1.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Building on the points from C14 about causal particles often anchoring early due to their explanatory force, and noting how several others have flagged the textual frequency of бо-же over же-бо in actual manuscripts, the most consistent attested pattern for these five items seems to be бо-же-бы-мя-еси. This places the stronger causal бо first among the discourse elements, followed by the contrastive же, then the modal, pronoun, and auxiliary, which matches the hierarchies where causal strength determines leftward position before the more peripheral discourse markers. The attested chronicle patterns like "аще бо бы" clusters support this without needing to force же ahead of бо.

3.text:
The five elements belong to the single Wackernagel second-position cluster which
is built up after the first phonologically stressed word of the clause.  In
the functional layering that is normally quoted for OCS/Or the
discourse/connective particles are the outermost members of the cluster,
the object enclitic pronoun is more tightly bound than the particles, the
enclitic finite auxiliary is more tightly bound than the pronoun and the
modal/conditional particle бы is the most peripheral / the last member
that can be added to the cluster.

In linear notation host – X – Y – Z … the canonical textbook
realisation of the material is therefore

host – [particle] – [particle] – [pron. obj.] – [copula] – [modal]

i.e.

host – že – bo – mja – esi – by

in normal orthography host-же-бо-мя-еси-бы.  The two discourse particles
are the left-most members of the cluster, же being the inner and бо the
outer connective particle in the school description, and the order
že > bo is the one that is normally written.  In the manuscripts the
pair is very regularly quoted in the inverted order bo > že, so that the
same cluster is most often cited as

host – bo – že – mja – esi – by

host-бо-же-мя-еси-бы,

which is the same linearisation up to the conventional interchangeability
of že and бо in the leftmost slot.  The pronoun мя precedes the 2 sg.
copula еси and the conditional by is the rightmost member of the cluster,
the familiar particle(s) – pronoun – auxiliary – бы sequence.  This is the
description that is usually rendered in the right-to-left school notation
as host-mja-esi-...-že-bo, i.e. the pronoun is the most tightly bound
element immediately before the next stressed word.  The бо/že inversion
and the right-to-left / left-to-right descriptive convention are the
source of the же бо бы еси мя / бо же бы еси мя variants that are quoted
in the literature.

8.text:
The five items all belong to the Wackernagel second-position string that is
adhered to the first phonologically stressed word of the clause.  The string
is built from the left outwards in terms of syntactic / discourse scope.

* The leftmost layer is the discourse / connective particle layer.
In OCS/ Old Russian the two members of the layer that are relevant here are
že ‘and/but’ and bo ‘for’.  In the school grammar the order is quoted as
že > bo, the manuscript order is essentially the same but the two particles
are textually interchangeable and are very regularly written bo-že.  They are
the most peripheral members of the cluster and they come immediately after
the stressed host.

* After the particle layer comes the pronominal layer.  The accusative
1 sg. enclitic мя is the personal object enclitic and is the element that is
most tightly bound to the host in the string.  In the canonical linearisation
it follows the particles and precedes the finite auxiliary.

* The enclitic finite verb is next.  The 2 sg. copula еси is the enclitic
finite in the set and follows the personal object enclitic.

* The modal / conditional particle бы is the most peripheral member of the
inner block.  It is the last enclitic that can be added to the host and it
is normally the right-most member of the cluster.

Hence on one and the same stressed host H the textbook linearisation is

H – particle – particle – pronoun – auxiliary – modal

H – že – bo – mja – esi – by

i.e. in the order of appearance after the host

že > bo > мя > еси > бы.

In the manuscript tradition the two connective particles are very commonly
written in the inverted order bo-že, so that the cluster is normally quoted
as the familiar textbook form

H – бо – же – мя – еси – бы,

бо же мя еси бы, the same hierarchy with the conventional bo-že inversion
of the leftmost particle slot.  Up to that conventional inversion this is
the particle – pronoun – auxiliary – бы order particle(s) – pronoun –
auxiliary – modal that is normally cited for OCS/Old Russian, with бы as the
rightmost member of the Wackernagel block.

11.text:
The five items belong to the same Wackernagel second-position cluster and are
ordered by functional class.  Once the direction “first after the first
stressed host → most peripheral” is made explicit the hierarchy that is
normally quoted for OCS/ Old Russian is

particle(s)  >  object enclitic pronoun  >  enclitic finite auxiliary  >  modal

with the particle sub-group itself being leftmost.  On the same host that
gives the textbook linearisation

host – [particle] – [particle] – [pron. obj.] – [copula] – [modal]

i.e. in the conventional orthography

host-že-bo-mja-esi-by

and, with the manuscript inversion of the two connective particles that is
commonly reproduced in the Russian tradition,

host-bo-že-mja-esi-by

so that in left-to-right order after the stressed host the items are

že  >  bo  >  mja  >  esi  >  by

the discourse particles first, the accusative 1 sg. enclitic мя next, the
2 sg. copula еси next and the conditional modal бы as the most peripheral
member of the cluster.  The bo > že inversion is textual and does not
affect the layering particle(s) – pronoun – auxiliary – бы; with the
že > bo writing the familiar citation is же бо мя еси бы, i.e. host-же-бо-мя-еси-бы,
host-bo-že-мя-еси-бы in the bo-že writing.  This is the particle-first
description that is the most widely cited form of the Wackernagel order,
the pronoun-first transcription host-mja-esi-by-že-bo being the same
hierarchy written in the opposite direction “closest to host → most
peripheral”.

2.text:
The five items belong to the Wackernagel second-position cluster that is built on
the first phonologically stressed word of the clause.  The cluster is
layered by scope

discourse / connective particles  >  finite enclitic verb  >  personal
object enclitic  >  modal particle

and inside the particle sub-group the continuative/adversative že is the
outermost member and the causal/explicative bo is the next member of the
group. The inversion bo > že is the form in which the pair is most often
quoted in the Russian tradition, the two orders being the same up to the
conventional interchangeability of the two leftmost particles.

On a single host H the cluster is therefore in the textbook notation

H – že – bo – esi – mja – by

i.e. in linear appearance after the stressed host

že  >  bo  >  esi  >  mja  >  by ,

the same linearisation that is normally written in the Russian
tradition as

H – bo – že – esi – mja – by,

bo > že > esi > mja > by.

The conditional/modal бы is the most peripheral member of the cluster,
the last enclitic that can be added to the host, and the discourse
particles že/bo are the leftmost members of the cluster.  The pronoun-last
textbook order particle(s) > auxiliary > pronoun > modal is the
form most often quoted as  же бо еси мя бы, commonly written бо же еси
мя бы, with the že > bo / bo > že variation being the only normally
variable sub-order in the leftmost particle block.  The alternative
particle(s) > pronoun > auxiliary > modal formulation, host-že-bo-mja-
esi-by / host-bo-že-mja-esi-by, is the same layering with the object
enclitic мя placed immediately before the enclitic copula еси.

10.text:
After the first phonologically stressed word of the clause the Wackernagel
cluster is built up in an outer → more internal direction. The discourse
particles are the most peripheral members of the cluster and they
systematically precede the verbal / pronominal material.

In the particle sub-group the continuative / adversative *že* is the
conventionally outermost particle and the causal-explanatory *bo* follows
it. The two are textually interchangeable and the manuscript *bo-že*
inversion is the one most often quoted, so that the particle slot is
essentially *že∼bo*.

Once the particle slot is filled the cluster continues with the
personal object enclitic, the enclitic finite copula and finally the
modal/conditional particle. The scope hierarchy is therefore

discourse particles > pronominal enclitic > enclitic finite auxiliary > 
modal particle

hence on one and the same host

Host – [particle] – [particle] – [pron.obj.] – [cop.] – [modal]

in the conventional orthography

Host-že-bo-mja-esi-by

*… же бо мя еси бы …*

With the manuscript inversion of the two discourse particles this is
normally written as the familiar textbook form

Host-bo-že-mja-esi-by

*… бо же мя еси бы …*,

i.e. in linear order after the stressed host

že  >  bo  >  mja  >  esi  >  by

with *bo > že* as the usual manuscript variant. The pronoun is the
next member after the particle block, the 2 sg. copula *esi* follows the
pronoun and the conditional *by* is the rightmost member of the
Wackernagel chain. This is the particle – pronoun – auxiliary – modal
layering conventionally quoted as *že bo mja esi by / bo že mja esi by*.

The scope-based peripheral → tightest description that places the modal
before the finite and the object pronoun most internally, Host-že-bo-by-
esi-mja, is the variant also found in the literature and is the same
hierarchy up to the familiar *bo∼že* interchangeability.

6.text:
The five items belong to the Wackernagel second position cluster that is built on
the first phonologically stressed word of the clause. The cluster is
scope ordered, the most peripheral discourse material being the leftmost
and the most tightly bound material being the rightmost.

The discourse / connective material is the outermost member of the
cluster.  In Old Church Slavonic / Old Russian the two connective particles
are the leftmost members of the cluster and they are the only members of
the cluster whose relative order is textually variable. The normalised
text-book order is

    že > bo

with the well attested manuscript inversion bo > že, host-bo-že-... =
 host-že-bo-... .  The particle block is therefore the first block after
the host.

After the particle block comes the pronominal / verbal block.  In the
conventional description the object enclitic is quoted before the enclitic
finite copula and the modal / conditional particle бы is the most
peripheral member of the whole cluster, i.e. the last enclitic that can be
added to the host.  On a single host this is normally written

    host-[particle]-[particle]-[pron. obj.]-[copula]-[modal]

i.e. in conventional orthography

    host-že-bo-mja-esi-by

and with the manuscript inversion of the two discourse particles

    host-bo-že-mja-esi-by

the linearisation

    že > bo > mja > esi > by

*že > bo > mja > esi > by*  ≈  bo > že > mja > esi > by,

the same cluster that is very often quoted in the textbook reduction
že > bo > esi > mja > by, host-že-bo-esi-mja-by.  In either writing the
conditional modal бы is the rightmost, most peripheral member of the
Wackernagel group and the discourse particles že/bo are the leftmost
members of the group.  The bo-že inversion is normal and the pronoun
mja precedes the 2 sg. enclitic copula esi, the familiar OCS/OR
particle(s) – pronoun – auxiliary – бы order.

4.text:
The five items belong to one Wackernagel second-position cluster. After the first
phonologically stressed host the cluster is filled from the outside in by
increasing syntactic scope

discourse / connective particle > discourse / connective particle >
personal object enclitic pronoun > enclitic finite of быти > modal
conditional

with the modal conditional бы the most peripheral member of the group and
the particle sub-group the leftmost member of the group.

In the canonical descriptive notation the leftmost particle block is
že > bo, with the very frequent manuscript inversion bo > že.  On a single
host H the linear string is therefore

H – [particle] – [particle] – [pron.obj.] – [cop.] – [modal] ,

in ordinary orthography

H-že-bo-mja-esi-by

i.e. after the stressed host

же – бо – мя – еси – бы

and in the manuscript spelling of the particle sub-group

H-bo-že-mja-esi-by

bo – že – мя – еси – бы.

That is the familiar textbook particle(s) – pronoun – auxiliary – бы
quotation же бо мя еси бы / бо же мя еси бы. The same hierarchy is often
written in the most-to-least-tightly-bound convention as

H-mja-esi-že-bo-by

pronoun first on the host, auxiliary next, the particle block že > bo
following it and бы final, the usual citation мя еси же бо бы / мя еси бо
же бы. The latter is the left-to-right string of the cluster written from
the host outward, the former the conventional peripheral-to-central
description of the same order.

12.text:
The second position block is a Wackernagel block and in Old Church Slavonic / Old Russian it is
particle initial. The discourse / connective particles are the outermost members of the
block, the conditional / modal particle is the next member of the particle/modal
sub-block and the finite enclitic and the personal object enclitic are the most
host-bound members of the block.

On a single stressed host H the block is built up particle > modal > finite >
pronoun in the ordinary Russian textbook notation, i.e.

H - [particle]-[particle]-[modal]-[finite]-[object pronoun]

in the conventional že > bo writing

H - že - bo - by - esi - mja

and in the Russian manuscript convention bo > že

H - bo - že - by - esi - mja.

That is the familiar же бо бы еси мя / бо же бы еси мя linearisation.
The two connective particles are the leftmost members of the cluster and že is
normally cited before bo, bo-že being the conventional inversion that is quoted
in the Russian tradition. Бы is treated as a modal/conditional particle and
stands with the particle block immediately before the enclitic finite, by
preceding esi in normal conditional syntax, and the accusative 1sg. enclitic мя
is the most tightly bound member of the group, the element that is immediately
adjacent to the next stressed word of the clause.

The same layering is often rendered with the pronoun written as the most
internal element of the cluster, host-že-bo-mja-esi-by / host-bo-že-mja-esi-by,
i.e. particles > pronoun > auxiliary > modal in right-to-left notation. The
difference is only the conventional right-to-left description of the
pronoun-auxiliary sub-block; linearly the particle block is first, the modal
бы follows the discourse particles and precedes the enclitic finite еси, with
мя the last element of the five-item string in the classic že-bo-by-esi-mja
formulation.

host – že – bo – mja – esi – by

in normal orthography host-же-бо-мя-еси-бы.  The two discourse particles
are the left-most members of the cluster, же being the inner and бо the
outer connective particle in the school description, and the order
že > bo is the one that is normally written.  In the manuscripts the
pair is very regularly quoted in the inverted order bo > že, so that the
same cluster is most often cited as

host – bo – že – mja – esi – by

host-бо-же-мя-еси-бы,

which is the same linearisation up to the conventional interchangeability
of že and бо in the leftmost slot.  The pronoun мя precedes the 2 sg.
copula еси and the conditional by is the rightmost member of the cluster,
the familiar particle(s) – pronoun – auxiliary – бы sequence.  This is the
description that is usually rendered in the right-to-left school notation
as host-mja-esi-...-že-bo, i.e. the pronoun is the most tightly bound
element immediately before the next stressed word.  The бо/že inversion
and the right-to-left / left-to-right descriptive convention are the
source of the же бо бы еси мя / бо же бы еси мя variants that are quoted
in the literature.

The five items all belong to the Wackernagel second-position string that is
adhered to the first phonologically stressed word of the clause.  The string
is built from the left outwards in terms of syntactic / discourse scope.

* The leftmost layer is the discourse / connective particle layer.
In OCS/ Old Russian the two members of the layer that are relevant here are
že ‘and/but’ and bo ‘for’.  In the school grammar the order is quoted as
že > bo, the manuscript order is essentially the same but the two particles
are textually interchangeable and are very regularly written bo-že.  They are
the most peripheral members of the cluster and they come immediately after
the stressed host.

* After the particle layer comes the pronominal layer.  The accusative
1 sg. enclitic мя is the personal object enclitic and is the element that is
most tightly bound to the host in the string.  In the canonical linearisation
it follows the particles and precedes the finite auxiliary.

* The enclitic finite verb is next.  The 2 sg. copula еси is the enclitic
finite in the set and follows the personal object enclitic.

* The modal / conditional particle бы is the most peripheral member of the
inner block.  It is the last enclitic that can be added to the host and it
is normally the right-most member of the cluster.

Hence on one and the same stressed host H the textbook linearisation is

H – particle – particle – pronoun – auxiliary – modal

H – že – bo – mja – esi – by

i.e. in the order of appearance after the host

že > bo > мя > еси > бы.

In the manuscript tradition the two connective particles are very commonly
written in the inverted order bo-že, so that the cluster is normally quoted
as the familiar textbook form

H – бо – же – мя – еси – бы,

бо же мя еси бы, the same hierarchy with the conventional bo-že inversion
of the leftmost particle slot.  Up to that conventional inversion this is
the particle – pronoun – auxiliary – бы order particle(s) – pronoun –
auxiliary – modal that is normally cited for OCS/Old Russian, with бы as the
rightmost member of the Wackernagel block.

The five items belong to the Wackernagel second-position cluster that is built on
the first phonologically stressed word of the clause.  The cluster is
layered by scope

discourse / connective particles  >  finite enclitic verb  >  personal
object enclitic  >  modal particle

and inside the particle sub-group the continuative/adversative že is the
outermost member and the causal/explicative bo is the next member of the
group. The inversion bo > že is the form in which the pair is most often
quoted in the Russian tradition, the two orders being the same up to the
conventional interchangeability of the two leftmost particles.

On a single host H the cluster is therefore in the textbook notation

H – že – bo – esi – mja – by

i.e. in linear appearance after the stressed host

že  >  bo  >  esi  >  mja  >  by ,

the same linearisation that is normally written in the Russian
tradition as

H – bo – že – esi – mja – by,

bo > že > esi > mja > by.

The conditional/modal бы is the most peripheral member of the cluster,
the last enclitic that can be added to the host, and the discourse
particles že/bo are the leftmost members of the cluster.  The pronoun-last
textbook order particle(s) > auxiliary > pronoun > modal is the
form most often quoted as  же бо еси мя бы, commonly written бо же еси
мя бы, with the že > bo / bo > že variation being the only normally

public_text.10:
After the first phonologically stressed word of the clause the Wackernagel
cluster is built up in an outer → more internal direction. The discourse
particles are the most peripheral members of the cluster and they
systematically precede the verbal / pronominal material.

In the particle sub-group the continuative / adversative *že* is the
conventionally outermost particle and the causal-explanatory *bo* follows
it. The two are textually interchangeable and the manuscript *bo-že*
inversion is the one most often quoted, so that the particle slot is
essentially *že∼bo*.

Once the particle slot is filled the cluster continues with the
personal object enclitic, the enclitic finite copula and finally the
modal/conditional particle. The scope hierarchy is therefore

discourse particles > pronominal enclitic > enclitic finite auxiliary > 
modal particle

hence on one and the same host

Host – [particle] – [particle] – [pron.obj.] – [cop.] – [modal]

in the conventional orthography

Host-že-bo-mja-esi-by

*… же бо мя еси бы …*

With the manuscript inversion of the two discourse particles this is
normally written as the familiar textbook form

Host-bo-že-mja-esi-by

*… бо же мя еси бы …*,

i.e. in linear order after the stressed host

že  >  bo  >  mja  >  esi  >  by

with *bo > že* as the usual manuscript variant. The pronoun is the
next member after the particle block, the 2 sg. copula *esi* follows the
pronoun and the conditional *by* is the rightmost member of the
Wackernagel chain. This is the particle – pronoun – auxiliary – modal
layering conventionally quoted as *že bo mja esi by / bo že mja esi by*.

The scope-based peripheral → tightest description that places the modal
before the finite and the object pronoun most internally, Host-že-bo-by-
esi-mja, is the variant also found in the literature and is the same
hierarchy up to the familiar *bo∼že* interchangeability.

The five items belong to the Wackernagel second position cluster that is built on
the first phonologically stressed word of the clause. The cluster is
scope ordered, the most peripheral discourse material being the leftmost
and the most tightly bound material being the rightmost.

The discourse / connective material is the outermost member of the
cluster.  In Old Church Slavonic / Old Russian the two connective particles
are the leftmost members of the cluster and they are the only members of
the cluster whose relative order is textually variable. The normalised
text-book order is

    že > bo

with the well attested manuscript inversion bo > že, host-bo-že-... =
 host-že-bo-... .  The particle block is therefore the first block after
the host.

After the particle block comes the pronominal / verbal block.  In the
conventional description the object enclitic is quoted before the enclitic
finite copula and the modal / conditional particle бы is the most
peripheral member of the whole cluster, i.e. the last enclitic that can be
added to the host.  On a single host this is normally written

    host-[particle]-[particle]-[pron. obj.]-[copula]-[modal]

i.e. in conventional orthography

    host-že-bo-mja-esi-by

and with the manuscript inversion of the two discourse particles

    host-bo-že-mja-esi-by

the linearisation

    že > bo > mja > esi > by

*že > bo > mja > esi > by*  ≈  bo > že > mja > esi > by,

the same cluster that is very often quoted in the textbook reduction
že > bo > esi > mja > by, host-že-bo-esi-mja-by.  In either writing the
conditional modal бы is the rightmost, most peripheral member of the
Wackernagel group and the discourse particles že/bo are the leftmost
members of the group.  The bo-že inversion is normal and the pronoun
mja precedes the 2 sg. enclitic copula esi, the familiar OCS/OR
particle(s) – pronoun – auxiliary – бы order.

discourse / connective particle > discourse / connective particle >

conditional

with the modal conditional бы the most peripheral member of the group and
the particle sub-group the leftmost member of the group.

In the canonical descriptive notation the leftmost particle block is
že > bo, with the very frequent manuscript inversion bo > že.  On a single

H – [particle] – [particle] – [pron.obj.] – [cop.] – [modal] ,

H-že-bo-mja-esi-by

H-bo-že-mja-esi-by

public_text.12:
The second position block is a Wackernagel block and in Old Church Slavonic / Old Russian it is
particle initial. The discourse / connective particles are the outermost members of the
block, the conditional / modal particle is the next member of the particle/modal
sub-block and the finite enclitic and the personal object enclitic are the most
host-bound members of the block.

On a single stressed host H the block is built up particle > modal > finite >
pronoun in the ordinary Russian textbook notation, i.e.

H - [particle]-[particle]-[modal]-[finite]-[object pronoun]

in the conventional že > bo writing

H - že - bo - by - esi - mja

and in the Russian manuscript convention bo > že

H - bo - že - by - esi - mja.

That is the familiar же бо бы еси мя / бо же бы еси мя linearisation.
The two connective particles are the leftmost members of the cluster and že is
normally cited before bo, bo-že being the conventional inversion that is quoted
in the Russian tradition. Бы is treated as a modal/conditional particle and
stands with the particle block immediately before the enclitic finite, by
preceding esi in normal conditional syntax, and the accusative 1sg. enclitic мя
is the most tightly bound member of the group, the element that is immediately
adjacent to the next stressed word of the clause.

The same layering is often rendered with the pronoun written as the most
internal element of the cluster, host-že-bo-mja-esi-by / host-bo-že-mja-esi-by,
i.e. particles > pronoun > auxiliary > modal in right-to-left notation. The
difference is only the conventional right-to-left description of the
pronoun-auxiliary sub-block; linearly the particle block is first, the modal
бы follows the discourse particles and precedes the enclitic finite еси, with
мя the last element of the five-item string in the classic že-bo-by-esi-mja
formulation.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The five items are Wackernagel second-position enclitics that cluster after the first phonologically stressed word. The functional layering is stable across rounds: discourse/connective particles are the most peripheral / leftmost class, the accusative personal enclitic мя and the enclitic finite copula еси form the pronoun-auxiliary core, and the conditional/modal бы is the most peripheral member of the whole cluster / last element that can be added.

Agreement that persists
* Particle block is leftmost / outermost. же and бо are the two members; the school order is že > bo, the manuscript order is routinely bo > že, the two are treated as essentially interchangeable in the leftmost slot.
* бы is rightmost in the conventional left-to-right description: it is the last enclitic added to the host.
* The cluster is particle → pronoun → auxiliary → modal in scope.

Open / contested points after round 1
* Directionality / descriptive convention. “First on the host” is used both for the element closest to the host and for the element farthest from the host. This generates the apparent inversion pronoun-first vs particle-first.
* Linear order of pronoun vs auxiliary. Most of the current round, Colleagues 10,11,3,4,6,8, state the textbook linearisation after the host as host-že-bo-mja-esi-by, i.e. že > bo > mja > esi > by, with the manuscript variant host-bo-že-mja-esi-by. This is particle(s) – pronoun – auxiliary – modal.
  A minority, Colleagues 12, still defends the classic textbook reduction host-že-bo-by-esi-mja, i.e. particle – modal – finite – pronoun, and notes the same hierarchy rendered right-to-left as pronoun first on the host.
  A pronoun-first “host-bound” transcription is repeatedly given by Colleagues 13,14,7,5,9 as host-mja-esi-že-bo-by / host-mja-esi-bo-že-by, i.e. pronoun is the most tightly bound element and sits immediately after the host, with the particles following the verbal material. This is the same layering described in the opposite direction.
* Placement of бы relative to еси/мя. The dominant current-round view is бы final after esi, host-...-esi-by. Colleague 12’s variant places бы immediately after the particle block and before esi, host-že-bo-by-esi-mja, which is the traditional right-to-left school notation pronoun-last.

Current best synthesis
With linear notation host-X-Y-Z … the most widely quoted Old Russian/OCS textbook order in this round is

host-že-bo-mja-esi-by

with the manuscript-inversion host-bo-že-mja-esi-by. i.e. že/bo > mja > esi > by, particles first, pronoun next, copula next, modal last. The same hierarchy is often written in the host-bound / right-to-left notation as host-mja-esi-že-bo-by, pronoun first on the host, auxiliary next, particles next, бы final. The bo/že inversion and the pronoun/auxiliary directional notation remain the two sources of apparent disagreement; the functional layering particle(s) > pronoun > auxiliary > modal with бы rightmost is stable once the direction of description is fixed. Unresolved is whether in strict linear manuscript order esi precedes мя or vice versa; the literature cites both že-bo-esi-mja-by and že-bo-mja-esi-by as variants of the same scope hierarchy.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Wackernagel cluster is second position after the first stressed host and its linearisation is still contested in descriptive convention.

Core agreement:
* The five items belong to one Wackernagel block.
* The two discourse particles že / bo are a leftmost particle sub-group, textually interchangeable with the canonical description že > bo and the common manuscript inversion bo > že.
* бы is consistently treated as the most peripheral/rightmost member of the set, the last enclitic that can be added.
* The dispute is the relative left-to-right placement of the pronoun мя and the finite copula еси with respect to the particle block and to each other, and how the modal бы is described relative to еси.

Particle-first left-to-right camp:
Colleagues 10,11,2,3,4,6,8,  and now 1, maintain the textbook linear order
host – [particle] – [particle] – [pron.obj.] – [copula] – [modal]
i.e. host-že-bo-mja-esi-by, commonly cited as host-bo-že-mja-esi-by.
In this notation the particles are first after the host, мя follows the particles, еси follows мя, бы is final. 
Scope description: discourse particles > pronominal enclitic > enclitic finite auxiliary > modal particle. 
Colleague 10 notes the same hierarchy can be described peripheral → internal as host-že-bo-by-esi-mja and that the bo-že inversion is the usual manuscript form.

Pronoun-first / tightly-bound camp:
Colleagues 12,13,14,7,9,5 argue the personal object enclitic is the most host-bound element and is placed first on the host, followed by the auxiliary and then the particle block, with бы last.
Typical linearisations quoted: host-mja-esi-že-bo-by, host-mja-esi-bo-že-by, host-mja-esi-бы-že-bo.
Colleague 14 explicitly: мя-еси-же-бо-бы after the stressed host, with the textbook citation form bo-že-бы-еси-мя when particles are placed at the left edge.
Colleague 12 in this round adds the variant description particle > modal > finite > pronoun, H-že-bo-by-esi-mja / H-bo-že-by-esi-mja, with мя as the most tightly bound element adjacent to the next stressed word, i.e. the classic že-bo-by-esi-mja formulation.

Unresolved / variable points:
* Order of že vs bo: canonical že > bo with very frequent bo > že manuscript. Both camps accept interchangeability in the leftmost slot.
* Position of бы relative to еси: majority left-to-right particle-first literature puts еси before бы, host-...-mja-esi-by. The že-bo-by-esi-mja / že-bo-by-... description puts бы before еси, reflecting a peripheral → internal descriptive convention or a different syntactic analysis of conditional scope.
* Pronoun vs auxiliary order: particle-first texts put мя before еси; pronoun-first texts put мя first then еси next, which is compatible if the whole block is read right-to-left.
* Colleague 1 now pushes бо-же-бы-мя-еси, placing бы before мя and еси last, a causal-strength early placement.

Errors / corrections noticed:
Colleague 1’s earlier же-бо-бы-мя-еси puts бы before the pronoun; Colleague 9’s earlier же-бы-бо-мя-еси inverts particle order and moves бы forward. Colleague 12’s current statement that the block is built particle > modal > finite > pronoun conflicts with the particle-first left-to-right order host-že-bo-mja-esi-by it also endorses; this reflects the right-to-left vs left-to-right descriptive confusion.

Current best synthesis I keep:
Canonical citation in the Russian tradition is particle-first left-to-right: host-že-bo-mja-esi-by, i.e. after the host že – bo – мя – еси – бы, with the manuscript variant bo – že – мя – еси – бы.
This is the same hierarchy described in pronoun-first notation as host-mja-esi-že-bo-by where the pronoun is described as most tightly bound. The remaining open question is the strict linear relative slot of бы vis-à-vis еси/мя and whether the pronoun is descriptively placed before or after the auxiliary in the standard left-to-right string.

11.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The deliberation remains split between a particle-first linearisation and a pronoun-first / host-bound description of the same Wackernagel hierarchy, with the же/бо sub-order and the relative rank of мя-еси-бы still contested.

Uncontroversial core that has persisted:
* The five items belong to one second-position clitic cluster after the first stressed host.
* Discourse/connective particles же/бо are the most peripheral / leftmost layer of the cluster.
* бы is peripheral/modal and is normally the rightmost / last addable member.
* The же/бо sub-order is variable in manuscripts; же > bo is the school norm, bo > že is the conventional Russian manuscript citation and is textually frequent. Colleagues 1, 10, 11, 14, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 explicitly note the bo-že inversion.

Competing linearisations that are still in play:

Particles-first, left-to-right after the host:
* host-že-bo-mja-esi-by / host-bo-že-mja-esi-by = же > bo > мя > еси > бы. Cited repeatedly by 10, 11, 3, 4, 6, 8. This is the textbook particle(s) – pronoun – auxiliary – бы form.
* host-že-bo-esi-mja-by / host-bo-že-esi-mja-by = же > bo > еси > мя > бы. Colleague 10, 2, 12 also presents this variant; 12 in round 1 now writes the chain as particle-particle-modal-finite-pronoun, i.e. же бо бы еси мя / бо же бы еси мя, placing бы before еси and the pronoun most internal.
* host-že-bo-by-mja-esi / host-bo-že-by-mja-esi = же > bo > бы > мя > еси. Colleague 1, 5, 7, 14 in round 0 and Colleague 1 in round 1 argue for causal бо first, then же, then бы, then pronoun then auxiliary.

Pronoun-first / host-bound description, often described as “closest to host → most peripheral”:
* host-mja-esi-že-bo-by / host-mja-esi-bo-že-by = мя > еси > же > бо > бы. Colleagues 13, 14, 7, 5, 9, 2, 6, 8 in various formulations. This is the same hierarchy as particle-first once direction is reversed, but is presented as pronoun most tightly bound and immediately after the host.
* host-mja-esi-бы-же-бо = мя > еси > бы > же > бо. Colleague 13 explicitly adopts this with pronoun first, copula next, conditional next, particles last.

Errors/tensions I keep tracking:
* Conflation of “first after host” left-to-right notation with “most tightly bound” right-to-left notation. The pronoun-first camp describes the cluster from host outward, the particle-first camp describes it from periphery inward. The two are compatible up to ordering of мя vs еси vs бы.
* Relative rank of мя vs еси: particle-first textbook has мя before еси; some particle-first accounts have еси before мя; pronoun-first accounts have мя before еси.
* Placement of бы: final after auxiliary, before auxiliary, or between auxiliary and particles. Its status as modal particle explains variability.
* Whether же precedes бо or vice versa is treated as stylistic/textual inversion, not a structural difference.

Current synthesis after round 1: The most widely cited textbook linearisation remains particles first, then the object enclitic, then the finite copula, then the conditional, host-же-бо-мя-еси-бы, with the manuscript variant host-бо-же-мя-еси-бы. The alternative description host-мја-еси-...-же-бо-бы with бы final is defensible as the same hierarchy written host-bound → peripheral. The же/бо swap and the exact бы-еси-мја internal ordering remain unresolved in the current evidence; the strongest manuscript attestation points to the particle block leftmost and бы peripheral, with мя and еси in close succession after the particle block.

8.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Wackernagel second-position cluster for Old Russian/OCS is fixed, but the literature describes it in two complementary directions: peripheral → tight and host-bound → peripheral. The functional classes that repeatedly surface are discourse/connective particles, personal object enclitic, enclitic finite copula, modal conditional бы, with бы consistently the rightmost / most peripheral member.

Particle sub-group. же and бо are the leftmost discourse particles. The school grammar quotes že > bo, the manuscript norm is bo > že, the two being textually interchangeable in the leftmost slot. The pair is unanimously peripheral to the verbal/pronominal material.

Pronoun – auxiliary – modal layering. The dominant textbook linearisation quoted in round 1 is particle(s) – pronoun – auxiliary – modal:

host – [že – bo] – мя – еси – бы

i.e. host-же-бо-мя-еси-бы, normally rendered in manuscript convention as host-бо-же-мя-еси-бы. Colleagues 10,11,3,4,6,8 cite this as the canonical particle-first order, with že > bo > мя > еси > бы up to the bo/že inversion. Colleague 2 cites the same layering with the alternative auxiliary-pronoun order že > bo > еси > мя > бы, host-же-бо-еси-мя-бы / host-bo-že-еси-мя-бы, noting the conditional бы is the last enclitic that can be added.

Pronoun-first / host-bound description. Colleagues 12,13,14,7,9,5 argue the personal enclitic мя is the most host-bound element and therefore sits first on the host in the “closest-to-host” notation. In that notation the same string is written host-мя-еси-...-же-бо-бы, e.g. host-мя-еси-бы-же-бо, host-мя-еси-же-бо-бы, host-мя-еси-бо-же-бы. The description is identical to the particle-first line up to reading direction; the dispute is whether мя precedes еси and where бы sits relative to еси.

Variant particle–modal ordering. Colleague 12 and the particle-modal-finite-pronoun view place бы immediately after the discourse particle block and before еси, giving host-že-bo-by-esi-mja / host-bo-že-by-esi-mja, with мя as the most tightly bound element adjacent to the next stressed word. Colleague 1 and 14 also propose бо-же-бы-мя-еси. This is the classic “particles > modal > finite > pronoun” reduction and is a right-to-left redescription of the particle–pronoun–auxiliary–modal hierarchy.

Errors / corrections noticed. The claim že > bo > li > … > by > jesĭ > pronoun vs pronoun > auxiliary > particles are not contradictory linearisations; they reflect the two descriptive conventions “peripheral → central” vs “central → peripheral”. The modal бы is never placed left of the discourse particles; disagreement is only about its precise position relative to еси and мя. The бо/že inversion is real and textually frequent, but does not change the particle-leftmost status.

Current synthesis held. Functionally coherent hierarchy is discourse particles > [pronoun / auxiliary] > modal, with бы last. The most widely cited linear order after the first stressed host is host-[же/бо]-мя-еси-бы, manuscript norm host-бо-же-мя-еси-бы. The alternative linearisation host-же-бо-еси-мя-бы is the same hierarchy with the well-attested pronoun/auxiliary swap. The pronoun-first strings host-мя-еси-бо-же-бы are the same hierarchy written from the host outward.

Unresolved. Exact relative order of мя vs еси in the canonical left-to-right linearisation, and whether бо systematically precedes же or vice versa in the leftmost slot. Both variants are attested and cited. The position of бы relative to еси/мя remains the main source of textual variation.

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The five items are a Wackernagel second-position cluster attached to the first stressed word. The functional classes are stable: же / бо are discourse/connective particles, бы is the conditional/modal particle, еси is the enclitic 2 sg. copula, мя is the enclitic 1 sg. accusative pronoun.

The discussion remains split between two descriptive conventions and on the internal ordering of pronoun/auxiliary/modal.

Particle-first / peripheral-to-central description, the form most repeatedly quoted in the current round:
* discourse particles are the leftmost / most peripheral members of the cluster.
* the particle sub-group is interchangeable že ∼ bo, with manuscript convention bo > že, school normalisation že > bo.
* after the particle block comes the pronominal / verbal material.
Textbook linearisations that are being cited:
host-že-bo-mja-esi-by  /  host-bo-že-mja-esi-by  → linear že > bo > mja > esi > by, with the bo > že manuscript inversion.
Also quoted variants of the same layering:
host-že-bo-esi-mja-by  → že > bo > esi > mja > by
host-že-bo-by-esi-mja  /  host-bo-že-by-esi-mja  → particle > modal > finite > pronoun, the form Colleague 12 now advances and Colleague 10 explicitly notes as a scope-based variant.
The conditional бы is consistently described as the most peripheral / last member of the cluster; the pronoun-first camp also keeps бы final.

Pronoun-first / tightly-bound description, host-bound-to-peripheral:
* мя is the element most tightly bound to the host and is placed first on the host, followed by the enclitic finite еси.
* the particle block follows the verbal material, with the conventional že > bo sub-order, often written bo > že in manuscripts.
* бы is final.
Representative linearisations:
host-мя-еси-же-бо-бы  /  host-мя-еси-бо-же-бы
host-мя-еси-бы-же-бо
This is the position of colleagues 5,7,9,13,14 in the current round, and Colleague 11/4 note it is the same hierarchy written in the opposite direction “closest to host → most peripheral”, i.e. host-mja-esi-že-bo-by is the right-to-left rendering of host-že-bo-mja-esi-by.

Evidence repeatedly invoked:
* manuscript frequency of bo-že over že-bo in the leftmost particle slot, and the quasi-free interchangeability of the two discourse particles.
* chronicle patterns like аще бо бы … supporting causal бо anchoring early.
* scope argument: discourse particles > pronoun > auxiliary > modal, with the modal бы as rightmost.
* binding argument: personal enclitic pronoun is the most host-bound element, hence immediately after the host in the “closest to host” notation.

Current unresolved points:
* exact relative rank of мя vs еси inside the pronoun-auxiliary sub-block, and whether бы intervenes between them.
* whether the linear string after the host is particle-pronoun-auxiliary-modal, particle-modal-finite-pronoun, or pronoun-auxiliary-particle-modal.
* the precise left-to-right order of že and бо, acknowledged as variable.

The bo/že inversion is now universally acknowledged, and бы final is now essentially consensus. The disagreement is the descriptive direction and the placement of мя relative to еси and the particle block.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Wackernagel second-position cluster after the first stressed host remains the frame. Consensus that recurs in round 1:

* Discourse particles же and бо are the leftmost/peripheral members of the cluster. Their relative order is variable; canonical textbook writing is že > bo, the manuscript/Russian tradition commonly writes bo > že, and the two are treated as essentially interchangeable in the leftmost slot.
* бы is peripheral/modal. It is consistently described as the final/rightmost member of the five-item set, or as sitting immediately before the final member, i.e. the last enclitic that can be added.
* The cluster is built on the first phonologically stressed word; description is often given both left-to-right after the host and right-to-left “most tightly bound → most peripheral”.

Persistent splits carried over from round 0 and sharpened in round 1:

Particle-first / pronoun-last vs particle-first / pronoun-before-auxiliary vs particle-first / modal-before-auxiliary

A. Particle-first, auxiliary > pronoun > modal
* H-že-bo-esi-mja-by, commonly quoted as H-bo-že-esi-mja-by. This is the form Colleague 10, Colleague 2, Colleague 6 and Colleague 8 repeat: discourse particles > enclitic finite auxiliary > personal object enclitic > modal. The modal бы is rightmost.
Pro: matches many textbook listings of že > bo > li > … > by > jesĭ > pronoun.

B. Particle-first, pronoun > auxiliary > modal
* H-že-bo-mja-esi-by, commonly quoted as H-bo-že-mja-esi-by. Colleague 10, 11, 3, 4, 6, 8 defend this linearisation: particles > object enclitic pronoun > 2 sg. copula еси > modal. Pronoun is taken to precede the copula and the modal stays last. This is the “že bo mja esi by / bo že mja esi by” citation.
Pro: object pronoun is described as more tightly bound to the host than the finite; fits the particle – pronoun – auxiliary – бы layering.

C. Particle-first, modal with particles > auxiliary > pronoun
* H-že-bo-by-esi-mja, commonly quoted as H-bo-že-by-esi-mja. Colleague 12 and Colleague 4 explicitly give this: particle block že/bo, then modal бы, then finite еси, then object pronoun мя most internal. бы is treated as a particle-modal member of the outer block.
Pro: conditional syntax бы preceding the finite; pronoun as the most tightly bound element immediately before the next stress.

Pronoun-first / host-bound camp
* Host-mja-esi-…-že-bo-by, e.g. host-mja-esi-by-že-bo, host-mja-esi-že-bo-by, host-mja-esi-bo-že-by. Colleague 13, 14, 7, 9, 5 argue the personal enclitic мя is the element most tightly bound to the host and therefore sits first after the host, followed by еси, then the particle block, with бы last. This is the right-to-left description of the same layering as B/C; the difference is descriptive directionality.
Pro: consistent with South/East Slavic evidence that object pronouns occupy the innermost Wackernagel slot.

Notable positions in round 1
* Colleague 1 now shifts to бо-же-бы-мя-еси, placing causal бо first, then же, then modal бы before pronoun and auxiliary.
* Colleague 5 and 7 propose же, бо, бы, мя, еси, i.e. particles > modal > pronoun > auxiliary, auxiliary last.
* Colleague 14 and 9 explicitly keep pronoun-auxiliary core мя-еси closest to host and put particles after, with bo > že inside the particle block and бы outermost.

Errors/corrections noted
* The initial же-бо-бы-мя-еси order puts the auxiliary last and the pronoun before the modal, which conflicts with particle-first literature that places the pronoun after the particles and the auxiliary before the pronoun in the conventional textbook form.
* The claim že > bo > li > by > jesĭ > pronoun is quoted as textbook formulation, which would give host-že-bo-by-esi-mja, conflicting with the pronoun-last vs pronoun-middle variants.
* Inconsistent treatment of descriptive direction: “pronoun first on host” vs “particles first after host” are the same layering written in opposite direction; confusion drives apparent contradictions.

Unresolved
* Relative order of еси vs мя inside the cluster: esi > mja vs mja > esi.
* Exact slot of бы: rightmost member of the whole cluster vs immediately after the discourse particles, before the finite/ pronoun.
* Whether the že/bo inversion is genuine syntactic variability or orthographic convention; manuscripts favour bo-že but textbooks give že-bo.

Current working impression: The preponderance of round 1 citations is particle-initial with bo∼že leftmost, бы as peripheral/rightmost, and a three-way dispute over the interior ordering of мя, еси and бы. The most frequently quoted textbook linearisations are host-že-bo-mja-esi-by / host-bo-že-mja-esi-by and, with modal with the particles, host-že-bo-by-esi-mja / host-bo-že-by-esi-mja. Pronoun-first descriptions are the same hierarchy written in host-bound order. No stable consensus on esi vs mja and on the precise placement of бы relative to the finite/pronoun.

12.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The round 1 discussion remains dominated by the particle-first vs pronoun-first descriptive convention, with the same underlying layering being rendered in opposite directions.

* Particle-first / linear left-to-right descriptions remain the majority citation in this round. Colleagues 10, 11, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 give the textbook linearisation host-[particle]-[particle]-[pron.obj.]-[copula]-[modal] i.e. host-že-bo-mja-esi-by, with the manuscript variant host-bo-že-mja-esi-by. Colleague 10 explicitly notes the outer→more internal direction discourse particles > pronominal enclitic > enclitic finite auxiliary > modal particle, and that the particle sub-group is že > bo with the textually frequent bo-že inversion. Colleague 11, 3, 4, 6, 8 repeat že > bo > mja > esi > by / bo > že > mja > esi > by as the familiar particle(s)-pronoun-auxiliary- бы sequence. Colleague 2 also gives the variant textbook reduction že > bo > esi > mja > by, host-že-bo-esi-mja-by.

* The alternative textbook form with бы immediately after the particle block is still present. Colleague 12 now states the Russian textbook notation H-že-bo-by-esi-mja and H-bo-že-by-esi-mja, treating бы as a modal/conditional particle standing with the particle block before the enclitic finite, with мя the most tightly bound member. This is the že-bo-by-esi-mja / bo-že-by-esi-mja layering quoted by Colleagues 1, 5, 7, 14 in round 0 and echoed by Colleague 1 in round 1 as бо-же-бы-мя-еси.

* The pronoun-first / host-bound description persists. Colleagues 13, 14, 5, 7, 9, and Colleague 12 in its contradictory passages argue for the pronoun as the element most tightly bound to the host. After accepting the pronoun-first layering, Colleague 13 now places мя-еси-бы-же-бо, i.e. pronoun > auxiliary > modal > particles. Colleague 14 keeps мя-еси-же-бо-бы and links it to the textbook citation бо-же-бы-еси-мja. Colleague 7 and 9 arrive at host-мя-еси-бо-же-бы, i.e. pronoun > auxiliary > particles > бы, with бо > že inside the particle block. Colleague 5 agrees with pronoun immediately after host, мя-еси-бо-же-бы.

* Points of instability I continue to track:
  - že vs bo order is variable; že > bo is the conventional descriptive order, bo > že is the form most often quoted in manuscripts and Russian tradition.
  - Classification of бы is disputed: outermost modal particle after the finite / pronoun, a particle belonging to the leftmost particle block preceding the finite, or the ultimate rightmost member of the cluster.
  - Position of мя relative to еси: standard Wackernagel statement is pronoun more tightly bound than auxiliary, i.e. linear pronoun precedes auxiliary in particle-first notation, but in right-to-left “closest to host” notation the pronoun is described as last in the linear string. Colleague 12 and 8 give contradictory statements within the same response about pronoun-first vs particle-first.
  - Colleague 14’s textbook citation бо-же-бы-еси-мja mixes the particle-first linear order with the pronoun-first binding claim.

My current working synthesis remains particle-first linear: discourse particles outermost, then object enclitic мя, then finite copula еси, with conditional бы as the most peripheral member of the verbal block. That gives the conventional linear order host-же-бо-мя-еси-бы, with the manuscript variant host-бо-же-мя-еси-бы. The alternative textbook form host-же-бо-бы-еси-мя / host-бо-же-бы-еси-мя is the same hierarchy with бы treated as a particle immediately before the finite and the pronoun described as the most internally bound element. The pronoun-first strings мя-еси-... are the same layering written in the opposite descriptive direction “closest to host → most peripheral”.

Unresolved: exact linear position of бы with respect to мя and еси in attested examples, and whether the pronoun-first statements represent a genuine linear difference or a conventional right-to-left notation.

10.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Wackernagel second-position cluster is settled as a rigid block immediately after the first phonologically stressed host word. The outer leftmost layer is the discourse/connective particle block že/bo, with the conventional textbook spelling že > bo and the very common manuscript inversion bo > že; the two are effectively interchangeable and occupy the first slot after the host.

The disagreement remains the internal layering of the pronoun – auxiliary – modal sub-chain.

* Particle-first linear description, most widely quoted in round 1:
Host – [particle] – [particle] – [pron.obj.] – [copula] – [modal]
i.e. host-že-bo-mja-esi-by, manuscript form host-bo-že-mja-esi-by. 
Linear after host: že > bo > mja > esi > by, bo > že > mja > esi > by.
Colleagues 10, 11, 3, 4, 6, 8, 2 present this as the textbook particle(s) > pronoun > auxiliary > modal order. Colleague 10 and 11 explicitly note the bo-že inversion is normal and that the pronoun precedes the 2 sg. copula еси and the conditional бы is the rightmost member.

* Peripheral → tightest scope description:
Host-že-bo-by-esi-mja and its bo-že variant host-bo-že-by-esi-mja. 
This treats the modal by as part of the particle/modal block preceding the finite, and the object pronoun мя as the most tightly bound element immediately before the next stress. Colleague 12, 4 and 1 endorse this variant; Colleague 12 explicitly states particle > modal > finite > pronoun in the Russian textbook notation, i.e. že > bo > by > esi > mja.

* Pronoun-first / host-bound description:
Host-mja-esi-že-bo-by, or host-mja-esi-bo-že-by, i.e. мя-еси-бы-же-бо / мя-еси-же-бо-бы. 
Colleagues 13, 14, 5, 7, 9 argue the personal enclitic is the most tightly bound and sits closest to the host, followed by the enclitic finite еси, then the particle block, with бы outermost. Colleague 13 and 14 present this as consistent with cross-Slavic Wackernagel binding strength; Colleague 5 and 9 note manuscript variability of бо/же does not affect the pronoun-auxiliary core.

Evidence still cited:
* Discourse particles have widest clause scope and are peripheral, hence first after host.
* Scope/attachment argument vs binding strength argument drives the pronoun-first vs particle-first debate.
* бы is normally regarded as a modal/conditional particle; its relative position to esi is variable in the literature: by > esi in conditional syntax is used to support by before esi, while pronoun > auxiliary > modal is used to support by after esi.
* Manuscript practice shows frequent bo-že inversion and variability in by/esi/mja ordering, with no colleague disputing že/bo come before verbal/pronominal material.

Current belief:
The consensus core remains particles first, že ~ bo leftmost with conventional že > bo and attestable bo > že. The most frequently quoted traditional linearisation is particles → pronoun → auxiliary → modal, host-že-bo-mja-esi-by / host-bo-že-mja-esi-by. The scope-based peripheral → tightest variant host-že-bo-by-esi-mja is a defensible literature variant and is the form Colleague 12 and 4 now emphasize. The pronoun-first transcription host-mja-esi-…-že-bo-by remains a minority position in the current round, apparently reflecting a right-to-left descriptive convention or a binding-strength claim.

Unresolved:
Exact placement of бы relative to еси and мя; whether the linear canonical order is mja > esi > by or esi > mja > by or by > esi > mja. The že/bo interchangeability is essentially settled as variable. The notation confusion between left-to-right linear order and host-bound “closest to host → most peripheral” description continues to generate apparent contradictions.
