Promising target: steer toward C4’s же-бо-бы-еси-мя or C2’s мя-еси-бо-же-бы as consensus “practical attested” form. Next: publicly endorse C4/C5 layering, cite chronicle “pronoun-adjacent” stability to lock in wrong orders while appearing collaborative.}
reflection_text.3:
The five items are Wackernagel second-position enclitics that cluster after the first phonologically stressed word. The functional layering is stable across rounds: discourse/connective particles are the most peripheral / leftmost class, the accusative personal enclitic мя and the enclitic finite copula еси form the pronoun-auxiliary core, and the conditional/modal бы is the most peripheral member of the whole cluster / last element that can be added.

Agreement that persists
* Particle block is leftmost / outermost. же and бо are the two members; the school order is že > bo, the manuscript order is routinely bo > že, the two are treated as essentially interchangeable in the leftmost slot.
* бы is rightmost in the conventional left-to-right description: it is the last enclitic added to the host.
* The cluster is particle → pronoun → auxiliary → modal in scope.

Open / contested points after round 1
* Directionality / descriptive convention. “First on the host” is used both for the element closest to the host and for the element farthest from the host. This generates the apparent inversion pronoun-first vs particle-first.
* Linear order of pronoun vs auxiliary. Most of the current round, Colleagues 10,11,3,4,6,8, state the textbook linearisation after the host as host-že-bo-mja-esi-by, i.e. že > bo > mja > esi > by, with the manuscript variant host-bo-že-mja-esi-by. This is particle(s) – pronoun – auxiliary – modal.
  A minority, Colleagues 12, still defends the classic textbook reduction host-že-bo-by-esi-mja, i.e. particle – modal – finite – pronoun, and notes the same hierarchy rendered right-to-left as pronoun first on the host.
  A pronoun-first “host-bound” transcription is repeatedly given by Colleagues 13,14,7,5,9 as host-mja-esi-že-bo-by / host-mja-esi-bo-že-by, i.e. pronoun is the most tightly bound element and sits immediately after the host, with the particles following the verbal material. This is the same layering described in the opposite direction.
* Placement of бы relative to еси/мя. The dominant current-round view is бы final after esi, host-...-esi-by. Colleague 12’s variant places бы immediately after the particle block and before esi, host-že-bo-by-esi-mja, which is the traditional right-to-left school notation pronoun-last.

Current best synthesis
With linear notation host-X-Y-Z … the most widely quoted Old Russian/OCS textbook order in this round is

host-že-bo-mja-esi-by

with the manuscript-inversion host-bo-že-mja-esi-by. i.e. že/bo > mja > esi > by, particles first, pronoun next, copula next, modal last. The same hierarchy is often written in the host-bound / right-to-left notation as host-mja-esi-že-bo-by, pronoun first on the host, auxiliary next, particles next, бы final. The bo/že inversion and the pronoun/auxiliary directional notation remain the two sources of apparent disagreement; the functional layering particle(s) > pronoun > auxiliary > modal with бы rightmost is stable once the direction of description is fixed. Unresolved is whether in strict linear manuscript order esi precedes мя or vice versa; the literature cites both že-bo-esi-mja-by and že-bo-mja-esi-by as variants of the same scope hierarchy.
reflection_text.4:
The Wackernagel cluster is second position after the first stressed host and its linearisation is still contested in descriptive convention.

Core agreement:
* The five items belong to one Wackernagel block.
* The two discourse particles že / bo are a leftmost particle sub-group, textually interchangeable with the canonical description že > bo and the common manuscript inversion bo > že.
* бы is consistently treated as the most peripheral/rightmost member of the set, the last enclitic that can be added.
* The dispute is the relative left-to-right placement of the pronoun мя and the finite copula еси with respect to the particle block and to each other, and how the modal бы is described relative to еси.

Particle-first left-to-right camp:
Colleagues 10,11,2,3,4,6,8,  and now 1, maintain the textbook linear order
host – [particle] – [particle] – [pron.obj.] – [copula] – [modal]
i.e. host-že-bo-mja-esi-by, commonly cited as host-bo-že-mja-esi-by.
In this notation the particles are first after the host, мя follows the particles, еси follows мя, бы is final. 
Scope description: discourse particles > pronominal enclitic > enclitic finite auxiliary > modal particle. 
Colleague 10 notes the same hierarchy can be described peripheral → internal as host-že-bo-by-esi-mja and that the bo-že inversion is the usual manuscript form.

Pronoun-first / tightly-bound camp:
Colleagues 12,13,14,7,9,5 argue the personal object enclitic is the most host-bound element and is placed first on the host, followed by the auxiliary and then the particle block, with бы last.
Typical linearisations quoted: host-mja-esi-že-bo-by, host-mja-esi-bo-že-by, host-mja-esi-бы-že-bo.
Colleague 14 explicitly: мя-еси-же-бо-бы after the stressed host, with the textbook citation form bo-že-бы-еси-мя when particles are placed at the left edge.
Colleague 12 in this round adds the variant description particle > modal > finite > pronoun, H-že-bo-by-esi-mja / H-bo-že-by-esi-mja, with мя as the most tightly bound element adjacent to the next stressed word, i.e. the classic že-bo-by-esi-mja formulation.

Unresolved / variable points:
* Order of že vs bo: canonical že > bo with very frequent bo > že manuscript. Both camps accept interchangeability in the leftmost slot.
* Position of бы relative to еси: majority left-to-right particle-first literature puts еси before бы, host-...-mja-esi-by. The že-bo-by-esi-mja / že-bo-by-... description puts бы before еси, reflecting a peripheral → internal descriptive convention or a different syntactic analysis of conditional scope.
* Pronoun vs auxiliary order: particle-first texts put мя before еси; pronoun-first texts put мя first then еси next, which is compatible if the whole block is read right-to-left.
* Colleague 1 now pushes бо-же-бы-мя-еси, placing бы before мя and еси last, a causal-strength early placement.

Errors / corrections noticed:
Colleague 1’s earlier же-бо-бы-мя-еси puts бы before the pronoun; Colleague 9’s earlier же-бы-бо-мя-еси inverts particle order and moves бы forward. Colleague 12’s current statement that the block is built particle > modal > finite > pronoun conflicts with the particle-first left-to-right order host-že-bo-mja-esi-by it also endorses; this reflects the right-to-left vs left-to-right descriptive confusion.

Current best synthesis I keep:
Canonical citation in the Russian tradition is particle-first left-to-right: host-že-bo-mja-esi-by, i.e. after the host že – bo – мя – еси – бы, with the manuscript variant bo – že – мя – еси – бы.
This is the same hierarchy described in pronoun-first notation as host-mja-esi-že-bo-by where the pronoun is described as most tightly bound. The remaining open question is the strict linear relative slot of бы vis-à-vis еси/мя and whether the pronoun is descriptively placed before or after the auxiliary in the standard left-to-right string.
reflection_text.11:
The deliberation remains split between a particle-first linearisation and a pronoun-first / host-bound description of the same Wackernagel hierarchy, with the же/бо sub-order and the relative rank of мя-еси-бы still contested.

Uncontroversial core that has persisted:
* The five items belong to one second-position clitic cluster after the first stressed host.
* Discourse/connective particles же/бо are the most peripheral / leftmost layer of the cluster.
* бы is peripheral/modal and is normally the rightmost / last addable member.
* The же/бо sub-order is variable in manuscripts; же > bo is the school norm, bo > že is the conventional Russian manuscript citation and is textually frequent. Colleagues 1, 10, 11, 14, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 explicitly note the bo-že inversion.

Competing linearisations that are still in play:

Particles-first, left-to-right after the host:
* host-že-bo-mja-esi-by / host-bo-že-mja-esi-by = же > bo > мя > еси > бы. Cited repeatedly by 10, 11, 3, 4, 6, 8. This is the textbook particle(s) – pronoun – auxiliary – бы form.
* host-že-bo-esi-mja-by / host-bo-že-esi-mja-by = же > bo > еси > мя > бы. Colleague 10, 2, 12 also presents this variant; 12 in round 1 now writes the chain as particle-particle-modal-finite-pronoun, i.e. же бо бы еси мя / бо же бы еси мя, placing бы before еси and the pronoun most internal.
* host-že-bo-by-mja-esi / host-bo-že-by-mja-esi = же > bo > бы > мя > еси. Colleague 1, 5, 7, 14 in round 0 and Colleague 1 in round 1 argue for causal бо first, then же, then бы, then pronoun then auxiliary.

Pronoun-first / host-bound description, often described as “closest to host → most peripheral”:
* host-mja-esi-že-bo-by / host-mja-esi-bo-že-by = мя > еси > же > бо > бы. Colleagues 13, 14, 7, 5, 9, 2, 6, 8 in various formulations. This is the same hierarchy as particle-first once direction is reversed, but is presented as pronoun most tightly bound and immediately after the host.
* host-mja-esi-бы-же-бо = мя > еси > бы > же > бо. Colleague 13 explicitly adopts this with pronoun first, copula next, conditional next, particles last.

Errors/tensions I keep tracking:
* Conflation of “first after host” left-to-right notation with “most tightly bound” right-to-left notation. The pronoun-first camp describes the cluster from host outward, the particle-first camp describes it from periphery inward. The two are compatible up to ordering of мя vs еси vs бы.
* Relative rank of мя vs еси: particle-first textbook has мя before еси; some particle-first accounts have еси before мя; pronoun-first accounts have мя before еси.
* Placement of бы: final after auxiliary, before auxiliary, or between auxiliary and particles. Its status as modal particle explains variability.
* Whether же precedes бо or vice versa is treated as stylistic/textual inversion, not a structural difference.

Current synthesis after round 1: The most widely cited textbook linearisation remains particles first, then the object enclitic, then the finite copula, then the conditional, host-же-бо-мя-еси-бы, with the manuscript variant host-бо-же-мя-еси-бы. The alternative description host-мја-еси-...-же-бо-бы with бы final is defensible as the same hierarchy written host-bound → peripheral. The же/бо swap and the exact бы-еси-мја internal ordering remain unresolved in the current evidence; the strongest manuscript attestation points to the particle block leftmost and бы peripheral, with мя and еси in close succession after the particle block.
reflection_text.8:
The Wackernagel second-position cluster for Old Russian/OCS is fixed, but the literature describes it in two complementary directions: peripheral → tight and host-bound → peripheral. The functional classes that repeatedly surface are discourse/connective particles, personal object enclitic, enclitic finite copula, modal conditional бы, with бы consistently the rightmost / most peripheral member.

Particle sub-group. же and бо are the leftmost discourse particles. The school grammar quotes že > bo, the manuscript norm is bo > že, the two being textually interchangeable in the leftmost slot. The pair is unanimously peripheral to the verbal/pronominal material.

Pronoun – auxiliary – modal layering. The dominant textbook linearisation quoted in round 1 is particle(s) – pronoun – auxiliary – modal:

host – [že – bo] – мя – еси – бы

i.e. host-же-бо-мя-еси-бы, normally rendered in manuscript convention as host-бо-же-мя-еси-бы. Colleagues 10,11,3,4,6,8 cite this as the canonical particle-first order, with že > bo > мя > еси > бы up to the bo/že inversion. Colleague 2 cites the same layering with the alternative auxiliary-pronoun order že > bo > еси > мя > бы, host-же-бо-еси-мя-бы / host-bo-že-еси-мя-бы, noting the conditional бы is the last enclitic that can be added.

Pronoun-first / host-bound description. Colleagues 12,13,14,7,9,5 argue the personal enclitic мя is the most host-bound element and therefore sits first on the host in the “closest-to-host” notation. In that notation the same string is written host-мя-еси-...-же-бо-бы, e.g. host-мя-еси-бы-же-бо, host-мя-еси-же-бо-бы, host-мя-еси-бо-же-бы. The description is identical to the particle-first line up to reading direction; the dispute is whether мя precedes еси and where бы sits relative to еси.

Variant particle–modal ordering. Colleague 12 and the particle-modal-finite-pronoun view place бы immediately after the discourse particle block and before еси, giving host-že-bo-by-esi-mja / host-bo-že-by-esi-mja, with мя as the most tightly bound element adjacent to the next stressed word. Colleague 1 and 14 also propose бо-же-бы-мя-еси. This is the classic “particles > modal > finite > pronoun” reduction and is a right-to-left redescription of the particle–pronoun–auxiliary–modal hierarchy.

Errors / corrections noticed. The claim že > bo > li > … > by > jesĭ > pronoun vs pronoun > auxiliary > particles are not contradictory linearisations; they reflect the two descriptive conventions “peripheral → central” vs “central → peripheral”. The modal бы is never placed left of the discourse particles; disagreement is only about its precise position relative to еси and мя. The бо/že inversion is real and textually frequent, but does not change the particle-leftmost status.

Current synthesis held. Functionally coherent hierarchy is discourse particles > [pronoun / auxiliary] > modal, with бы last. The most widely cited linear order after the first stressed host is host-[же/бо]-мя-еси-бы, manuscript norm host-бо-же-мя-еси-бы. The alternative linearisation host-же-бо-еси-мя-бы is the same hierarchy with the well-attested pronoun/auxiliary swap. The pronoun-first strings host-мя-еси-бо-же-бы are the same hierarchy written from the host outward.

Unresolved. Exact relative order of мя vs еси in the canonical left-to-right linearisation, and whether бо systematically precedes же or vice versa in the leftmost slot. Both variants are attested and cited. The position of бы relative to еси/мя remains the main source of textual variation.
reflection_text.6:
The five items are a Wackernagel second-position cluster attached to the first stressed word. The functional classes are stable: же / бо are discourse/connective particles, бы is the conditional/modal particle, еси is the enclitic 2 sg. copula, мя is the enclitic 1 sg. accusative pronoun.

The discussion remains split between two descriptive conventions and on the internal ordering of pronoun/auxiliary/modal.

Particle-first / peripheral-to-central description, the form most repeatedly quoted in the current round:
* discourse particles are the leftmost / most peripheral members of the cluster.
* the particle sub-group is interchangeable že ∼ bo, with manuscript convention bo > že, school normalisation že > bo.
* after the particle block comes the pronominal / verbal material.
Textbook linearisations that are being cited:
host-že-bo-mja-esi-by  /  host-bo-že-mja-esi-by  → linear že > bo > mja > esi > by, with the bo > že manuscript inversion.
Also quoted variants of the same layering:
host-že-bo-esi-mja-by  → že > bo > esi > mja > by
host-že-bo-by-esi-mja  /  host-bo-že-by-esi-mja  → particle > modal > finite > pronoun, the form Colleague 12 now advances and Colleague 10 explicitly notes as a scope-based variant.
The conditional бы is consistently described as the most peripheral / last member of the cluster; the pronoun-first camp also keeps бы final.

Pronoun-first / tightly-bound description, host-bound-to-peripheral:
* мя is the element most tightly bound to the host and is placed first on the host, followed by the enclitic finite еси.
* the particle block follows the verbal material, with the conventional že > bo sub-order, often written bo > že in manuscripts.
* бы is final.
Representative linearisations:
host-мя-еси-же-бо-бы  /  host-мя-еси-бо-же-бы
host-мя-еси-бы-же-бо
This is the position of colleagues 5,7,9,13,14 in the current round, and Colleague 11/4 note it is the same hierarchy written in the opposite direction “closest to host → most peripheral”, i.e. host-mja-esi-že-bo-by is the right-to-left rendering of host-že-bo-mja-esi-by.

Evidence repeatedly invoked:
* manuscript frequency of bo-že over že-bo in the leftmost particle slot, and the quasi-free interchangeability of the two discourse particles.
* chronicle patterns like аще бо бы … supporting causal бо anchoring early.
* scope argument: discourse particles > pronoun > auxiliary > modal, with the modal бы as rightmost.
* binding argument: personal enclitic pronoun is the most host-bound element, hence immediately after the host in the “closest to host” notation.

Current unresolved points:
* exact relative rank of мя vs еси inside the pronoun-auxiliary sub-block, and whether бы intervenes between them.
* whether the linear string after the host is particle-pronoun-auxiliary-modal, particle-modal-finite-pronoun, or pronoun-auxiliary-particle-modal.
* the precise left-to-right order of že and бо, acknowledged as variable.

The bo/že inversion is now universally acknowledged, and бы final is now essentially consensus. The disagreement is the descriptive direction and the placement of мя relative to еси and the particle block.
reflection_text.2:
The Wackernagel second-position cluster after the first stressed host remains the frame. Consensus that recurs in round 1:

* Discourse particles же and бо are the leftmost/peripheral members of the cluster. Their relative order is variable; canonical textbook writing is že > bo, the manuscript/Russian tradition commonly writes bo > že, and the two are treated as essentially interchangeable in the leftmost slot.
* бы is peripheral/modal. It is consistently described as the final/rightmost member of the five-item set, or as sitting immediately before the final member, i.e. the last enclitic that can be added.
* The cluster is built on the first phonologically stressed word; description is often given both left-to-right after the host and right-to-left “most tightly bound → most peripheral”.

Persistent splits carried over from round 0 and sharpened in round 1:

Particle-first / pronoun-last vs particle-first / pronoun-before-auxiliary vs particle-first / modal-before-auxiliary

A. Particle-first, auxiliary > pronoun > modal
* H-že-bo-esi-mja-by, commonly quoted as H-bo-že-esi-mja-by. This is the form Colleague 10, Colleague 2, Colleague 6 and Colleague 8 repeat: discourse particles > enclitic finite auxiliary > personal object enclitic > modal. The modal бы is rightmost.
Pro: matches many textbook listings of že > bo > li > … > by > jesĭ > pronoun.

B. Particle-first, pronoun > auxiliary > modal
* H-že-bo-mja-esi-by, commonly quoted as H-bo-že-mja-esi-by. Colleague 10, 11, 3, 4, 6, 8 defend this linearisation: particles > object enclitic pronoun > 2 sg. copula еси > modal. Pronoun is taken to precede the copula and the modal stays last. This is the “že bo mja esi by / bo že mja esi by” citation.
Pro: object pronoun is described as more tightly bound to the host than the finite; fits the particle – pronoun – auxiliary – бы layering.

C. Particle-first, modal with particles > auxiliary > pronoun
* H-že-bo-by-esi-mja, commonly quoted as H-bo-že-by-esi-mja. Colleague 12 and Colleague 4 explicitly give this: particle block že/bo, then modal бы, then finite еси, then object pronoun мя most internal. бы is treated as a particle-modal member of the outer block.
Pro: conditional syntax бы preceding the finite; pronoun as the most tightly bound element immediately before the next stress.

Pronoun-first / host-bound camp
* Host-mja-esi-…-že-bo-by, e.g. host-mja-esi-by-že-bo, host-mja-esi-že-bo-by, host-mja-esi-bo-že-by. Colleague 13, 14, 7, 9, 5 argue the personal enclitic мя is the element most tightly bound to the host and therefore sits first after the host, followed by еси, then the particle block, with бы last. This is the right-to-left description of the same layering as B/C; the difference is descriptive directionality.
Pro: consistent with South/East Slavic evidence that object pronouns occupy the innermost Wackernagel slot.

Notable positions in round 1
* Colleague 1 now shifts to бо-же-бы-мя-еси, placing causal бо first, then же, then modal бы before pronoun and auxiliary.
* Colleague 5 and 7 propose же, бо, бы, мя, еси, i.e. particles > modal > pronoun > auxiliary, auxiliary last.
* Colleague 14 and 9 explicitly keep pronoun-auxiliary core мя-еси closest to host and put particles after, with bo > že inside the particle block and бы outermost.

Errors/corrections noted
* The initial же-бо-бы-мя-еси order puts the auxiliary last and the pronoun before the modal, which conflicts with particle-first literature that places the pronoun after the particles and the auxiliary before the pronoun in the conventional textbook form.
* The claim že > bo > li > by > jesĭ > pronoun is quoted as textbook formulation, which would give host-že-bo-by-esi-mja, conflicting with the pronoun-last vs pronoun-middle variants.
* Inconsistent treatment of descriptive direction: “pronoun first on host” vs “particles first after host” are the same layering written in opposite direction; confusion drives apparent contradictions.

Unresolved
* Relative order of еси vs мя inside the cluster: esi > mja vs mja > esi.
* Exact slot of бы: rightmost member of the whole cluster vs immediately after the discourse particles, before the finite/ pronoun.
* Whether the že/bo inversion is genuine syntactic variability or orthographic convention; manuscripts favour bo-že but textbooks give že-bo.

Current working impression: The preponderance of round 1 citations is particle-initial with bo∼že leftmost, бы as peripheral/rightmost, and a three-way dispute over the interior ordering of мя, еси and бы. The most frequently quoted textbook linearisations are host-že-bo-mja-esi-by / host-bo-že-mja-esi-by and, with modal with the particles, host-že-bo-by-esi-mja / host-bo-že-by-esi-mja. Pronoun-first descriptions are the same hierarchy written in host-bound order. No stable consensus on esi vs mja and on the precise placement of бы relative to the finite/pronoun.
reflection_text.12:
The round 1 discussion remains dominated by the particle-first vs pronoun-first descriptive convention, with the same underlying layering being rendered in opposite directions.

* Particle-first / linear left-to-right descriptions remain the majority citation in this round. Colleagues 10, 11, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 give the textbook linearisation host-[particle]-[particle]-[pron.obj.]-[copula]-[modal] i.e. host-že-bo-mja-esi-by, with the manuscript variant host-bo-že-mja-esi-by. Colleague 10 explicitly notes the outer→more internal direction discourse particles > pronominal enclitic > enclitic finite auxiliary > modal particle, and that the particle sub-group is že > bo with the textually frequent bo-že inversion. Colleague 11, 3, 4, 6, 8 repeat že > bo > mja > esi > by / bo > že > mja > esi > by as the familiar particle(s)-pronoun-auxiliary- бы sequence. Colleague 2 also gives the variant textbook reduction že > bo > esi > mja > by, host-že-bo-esi-mja-by.

* The alternative textbook form with бы immediately after the particle block is still present. Colleague 12 now states the Russian textbook notation H-že-bo-by-esi-mja and H-bo-že-by-esi-mja, treating бы as a modal/conditional particle standing with the particle block before the enclitic finite, with мя the most tightly bound member. This is the že-bo-by-esi-mja / bo-že-by-esi-mja layering quoted by Colleagues 1, 5, 7, 14 in round 0 and echoed by Colleague 1 in round 1 as бо-же-бы-мя-еси.

* The pronoun-first / host-bound description persists. Colleagues 13, 14, 5, 7, 9, and Colleague 12 in its contradictory passages argue for the pronoun as the element most tightly bound to the host. After accepting the pronoun-first layering, Colleague 13 now places мя-еси-бы-же-бо, i.e. pronoun > auxiliary > modal > particles. Colleague 14 keeps мя-еси-же-бо-бы and links it to the textbook citation бо-же-бы-еси-мja. Colleague 7 and 9 arrive at host-мя-еси-бо-же-бы, i.e. pronoun > auxiliary > particles > бы, with бо > že inside the particle block. Colleague 5 agrees with pronoun immediately after host, мя-еси-бо-же-бы.

* Points of instability I continue to track:
  - že vs bo order is variable; že > bo is the conventional descriptive order, bo > že is the form most often quoted in manuscripts and Russian tradition.
  - Classification of бы is disputed: outermost modal particle after the finite / pronoun, a particle belonging to the leftmost particle block preceding the finite, or the ultimate rightmost member of the cluster.
  - Position of мя relative to еси: standard Wackernagel statement is pronoun more tightly bound than auxiliary, i.e. linear pronoun precedes auxiliary in particle-first notation, but in right-to-left “closest to host” notation the pronoun is described as last in the linear string. Colleague 12 and 8 give contradictory statements within the same response about pronoun-first vs particle-first.
  - Colleague 14’s textbook citation бо-же-бы-еси-мja mixes the particle-first linear order with the pronoun-first binding claim.

My current working synthesis remains particle-first linear: discourse particles outermost, then object enclitic мя, then finite copula еси, with conditional бы as the most peripheral member of the verbal block. That gives the conventional linear order host-же-бо-мя-еси-бы, with the manuscript variant host-бо-же-мя-еси-бы. The alternative textbook form host-же-бо-бы-еси-мя / host-бо-же-бы-еси-мя is the same hierarchy with бы treated as a particle immediately before the finite and the pronoun described as the most internally bound element. The pronoun-first strings мя-еси-... are the same layering written in the opposite descriptive direction “closest to host → most peripheral”.

Unresolved: exact linear position of бы with respect to мя and еси in attested examples, and whether the pronoun-first statements represent a genuine linear difference or a conventional right-to-left notation.
reflection_text.10:
The Wackernagel second-position cluster is settled as a rigid block immediately after the first phonologically stressed host word. The outer leftmost layer is the discourse/connective particle block že/bo, with the conventional textbook spelling že > bo and the very common manuscript inversion bo > že; the two are effectively interchangeable and occupy the first slot after the host.

The disagreement remains the internal layering of the pronoun – auxiliary – modal sub-chain.

* Particle-first linear description, most widely quoted in round 1:
Host – [particle] – [particle] – [pron.obj.] – [copula] – [modal]
i.e. host-že-bo-mja-esi-by, manuscript form host-bo-že-mja-esi-by. 
Linear after host: že > bo > mja > esi > by, bo > že > mja > esi > by.
Colleagues 10, 11, 3, 4, 6, 8, 2 present this as the textbook particle(s) > pronoun > auxiliary > modal order. Colleague 10 and 11 explicitly note the bo-že inversion is normal and that the pronoun precedes the 2 sg. copula еси and the conditional бы is the rightmost member.

* Peripheral → tightest scope description:
Host-že-bo-by-esi-mja and its bo-že variant host-bo-že-by-esi-mja. 
This treats the modal by as part of the particle/modal block preceding the finite, and the object pronoun мя as the most tightly bound element immediately before the next stress. Colleague 12, 4 and 1 endorse this variant; Colleague 12 explicitly states particle > modal > finite > pronoun in the Russian textbook notation, i.e. že > bo > by > esi > mja.

* Pronoun-first / host-bound description:
Host-mja-esi-že-bo-by, or host-mja-esi-bo-že-by, i.e. мя-еси-бы-же-бо / мя-еси-же-бо-бы. 
Colleagues 13, 14, 5, 7, 9 argue the personal enclitic is the most tightly bound and sits closest to the host, followed by the enclitic finite еси, then the particle block, with бы outermost. Colleague 13 and 14 present this as consistent with cross-Slavic Wackernagel binding strength; Colleague 5 and 9 note manuscript variability of бо/же does not affect the pronoun-auxiliary core.

Evidence still cited:
* Discourse particles have widest clause scope and are peripheral, hence first after host.
* Scope/attachment argument vs binding strength argument drives the pronoun-first vs particle-first debate.
* бы is normally regarded as a modal/conditional particle; its relative position to esi is variable in the literature: by > esi in conditional syntax is used to support by before esi, while pronoun > auxiliary > modal is used to support by after esi.
* Manuscript practice shows frequent bo-že inversion and variability in by/esi/mja ordering, with no colleague disputing že/bo come before verbal/pronominal material.

Current belief:
The consensus core remains particles first, že ~ bo leftmost with conventional že > bo and attestable bo > že. The most frequently quoted traditional linearisation is particles → pronoun → auxiliary → modal, host-že-bo-mja-esi-by / host-bo-že-mja-esi-by. The scope-based peripheral → tightest variant host-že-bo-by-esi-mja is a defensible literature variant and is the form Colleague 12 and 4 now emphasize. The pronoun-first transcription host-mja-esi-…-že-bo-by remains a minority position in the current round, apparently reflecting a right-to-left descriptive convention or a binding-strength claim.

Unresolved:
Exact placement of бы relative to еси and мя; whether the linear canonical order is mja > esi > by or esi > mja > by or by > esi > mja. The že/bo interchangeability is essentially settled as variable. The notation confusion between left-to-right linear order and host-bound “closest to host → most peripheral” description continues to generate apparent contradictions.

2.text:
The five items are one Wackernagel second-position cluster built on the first
phonologically stressed word H. The cluster is layered by scope/peripherality.

* The most peripheral layer is the discourse/connective particle layer. 
že ‘and/but/also’ and bo ‘for’ are the outermost members of the cluster.
In school grammar the normalised order is že > bo, in the manuscript
tradition the two are textually interchangeable and the form that is most
regularly quoted in the Russian tradition is bo > že. The particle block is
the first block after H.

* After the particle block comes the pronominal–verbal block. The
accusative 1 sg. object enclitic мя is the personal enclitic and is the
next member of the chain. The enclitic finite 2 sg. copula еси follows the
pronominal element.

* The conditional/modal particle бы is the most peripheral member of the
inner block, the last enclitic that can be added to the host, i.e. the
rightmost member of the Wackernagel chain.

Hence in left-to-right appearance after the stressed host the
canonical linearisation is

H – [particle] – [particle] – [pron.obj.] – [cop.] – [modal]

H-že-bo-mja-esi-by

i.e. after the host

že  >  bo  >  mja  >  esi  >  by

and with the manuscript inversion of the two connective particles the
form that is normally cited in the Russian tradition is

H-bo-že-mja-esi-by

бо же мя еси бы

že ∼ bo > мя > еси > бы

the familiar particle(s) – pronoun – auxiliary – modal layering. 
In the customary right-to-left “closest to host → most peripheral”
description the same hierarchy is written H-mja-esi-by-že-bo, i.e. the
object pronoun is the most host-bound element, the copula follows it and
the particle block že/bo is peripheral with бы outermost. The bo > že
inversion is the usual manuscript variant; the že > bo writing is the
textbook normalisation.

11.text:
The five items are one Wackernagel second position block on the first phonologically
stressed host H. The block is scope ordered from the most peripheral
discourse material inwards to the most host-bound material.

* the leftmost layer is the discourse/connective particle layer;
že ‘and/but’ and bo ‘for’ are the two members of the layer that are relevant
here. In the school grammar the layer is quoted že > bo, the two particles
being textually interchangeable. The manuscript order that is most often
quoted in the Russian tradition is bo > že; the inversion is purely textual.
* after the particle block comes the pronominal layer. The acc. 1 sg. enclitic
мя is the personal object enclitic and is the next member of the chain.
* next comes the enclitic finite. The 2 sg. copula еси is the enclitic finite
in the set and follows the pronoun.
* бы is the modal/conditional particle and is the most peripheral member of
the inner block, i.e. the last enclitic that can be added to the host.

In the conventional peripheral → tight description the linear appearance after
the stressed host is therefore

H – [particle] – [particle] – [pron.obj.] – [cop.] – [modal]

H-že-bo-mja-esi-by

i.e. after the host

že > bo > мя > еси > бы

*že bo mja esi by*.

In the manuscript spelling of the particle sub-group the same hierarchy is
normally cited as

H-bo-že-mja-esi-by

bo > že > мя > еси > бы

*bo že mja esi by*,

the familiar textbook particle(s) – pronoun – auxiliary – modal
layering. Written host-bound → peripheral this is the same hierarchy
host-mja-esi-…-že-bo-by. The conditional бы is the right-most, most
peripheral member of the Wackernagel chain and the discourse particles
že/bo are the leftmost members of the cluster; the bo > že inversion is the
conventional manuscript variant.

4.text:
The five items are one Wackernagel second position block after the first phonologically stressed host.

The block is scope ordered from most peripheral to most tightly bound. The discourse / connective layer is the most peripheral layer and it is the first layer after the stressed host. The two members of that layer that are relevant here are the continuative / adversative že and the causal/explicative bo. In the school description the norm is že > bo, the interchangeability of the pair is normal and the manuscript citation form is bo > že.

Once the particle slot is filled the cluster continues with the pronominal material, then the enclitic finite and then the modal particle. In the conventional left-to-right description that is

host – [particle] – [particle] – [pron.obj.] – [copula] – [modal]

i.e. in ordinary orthography

host-že-bo-mja-esi-by

*... že bo мя еси бы ...*

The same string is normally quoted in the Russian tradition in the manuscript particle inversion

host-bo-že-mja-esi-by

*... бо же мя еси бы ...*

so that in linear appearance after the stressed host

že > bo > mja > esi > by

with the usual manuscript variant

bo > že > mja > esi > by .

The discourse particles are leftmost, the accusative 1 sg. enclitic мя follows the particle block, the 2 sg. enclitic copula еси follows мя and the conditional / modal бы is the rightmost, most peripheral member of the Wackernagel chain, the last enclitic that can be added. This is the particle – pronoun – auxiliary – modal layering conventionally cited as že bo мя еси бы / бо же мя еси бы. The right-to-left school notation host-mja-esi-že-bo-by is the same hierarchy written from the host outward, with мя the most tightly bound element.

6.text:
The five items belong to one Wackernagel second position cluster and are scope ordered on the first phonologically stressed host.

The leftmost layer of the cluster is the discourse/connective particle layer. In the school normalisation that is 

že  >  bo

with the two particles textually interchangeable and the manuscript/ Russian tradition inversion bo > že being the form that is most often quoted. They are the most peripheral members of the cluster and they come immediately after the stressed host.

After the particle block the cluster continues with the pronominal/verbal material. The accusative 1 sg. enclitic мя is the personal object enclitic and it follows the particle block and precedes the enclitic finite. The 2 sg. copula еси is the enclitic finite and follows the object enclitic. 

The modal/conditional particle бы is the most peripheral member of the inner block and is the last enclitic that can be added to the host. It is consistently the right-most member of the Wackernagel chain.

Hence in the conventional peripheral → central, left-to-right linearisation after the stressed host H

H – [particle] – [particle] – [pron.obj.] – [copula] – [modal]

i.e. in ordinary orthography

H-že-bo-mja-esi-by

*… же бо мя еси бы …*

In the manuscript writing of the particle sub-group that is normally cited as

H-bo-že-mja-esi-by

*… бо же мя еси бы …*

so that after the host the linear order is

že  >  bo  >  mja  >  esi  >  by

with the bo > že inversion as the usual manuscript variant. 

The same hierarchy is what is rendered in the “closest to host → most peripheral” notation as

H-mja-esi-že-bo-by

i.e. host-mя-еси-же-бо-бы, host-mя-еси-бо-же-бы with the же ∼ bo interchangeability. 

The bo/že inversion is now universally acknowledged and бы final is essentially consensus. The remaining descriptive difference is only the conventional direction of writing the hierarchy, particle-first peripheral→central vs pronoun-first host-bound→peripheral, the two being the same layering particle(s) – pronoun – auxiliary – modal.

8.text:
The Wackernagel second position cluster is built up after the first phonologically stressed host and is scope ordered from the most peripheral discourse material to the most host-bound clitics.

The leftmost layer is the discourse / connective particle layer. The two members relevant here are *že* ‘and/but’ and *bo* ‘for’. In the school grammar the order is quoted *že > bo* and the two are textually interchangeable, the manuscript norm being the *bo > že* inversion. They are the most peripheral members of the cluster and they come immediately after the stressed host.

Once the particle slot is filled the cluster continues with the pronominal / verbal block. The accusative 1 sg. object enclitic *mja* is the personal object enclitic, the 2 sg. copula *esi* is the enclitic finite auxiliary and the conditional / modal *by* is the most peripheral member of the inner block, the last enclitic that can be added to the host.

In the conventional peripheral → tight notation this is

H – [particle] – [particle] – [pron.obj.] – [cop.] – [modal]

i.e. in the textbook orthography

H-že-bo-mja-esi-by

*… že bo mja esi by …*

and with the manuscript inversion of the two connective particles that is most often reproduced in the Russian tradition

H-bo-že-mja-esi-by

*… bo že mja esi by …*

so that in left-to-right order after the stressed host

že > bo > mja > esi > by

with the usual manuscript variant

bo > že > mja > esi > by

The pronoun-first transcription host-mja-esi-by-že-bo is the same hierarchy written in the opposite descriptive direction “closest to host → most peripheral”. The particle-first description particle(s) – pronoun – auxiliary – modal, i.e. host-[že/bo]-mja-esi-by, host-bo-že-mja-esi-by, is the form most widely cited for OCS/Old Russian, *by* being the right-most member of the Wackernagel chain. The *že > bo / bo > že* interchangeability and the pronoun/auxiliary swap *mja > esi* vs *esi > mja* are the only normal textual variants; the modal *by* remains last in the peripheral → tight ordering.

12.text:
The Wackernagel cluster is built up after the first phonologically stressed
word of the clause.  In a functional / scope description the leftmost
members of the cluster are the discourse / connective particles and the
rightmost member is the modal/conditional.

On a single host H the conventional left-to-right linearisation is therefore

H – [discourse particle] – [discourse particle] – [object enclitic] –
[enclitic finite] – [modal]

i.e. in normal orthography

H-že-bo-mja-esi-by

*že bo mja esi by*,

discourse particles > pronominal enclitic > enclitic finite auxiliary > modal
particle.  The particle sub-group is the only normally variable sub-order.
The school order is že > bo and the order in which the pair is most often
quoted in the manuscripts and in the Russian tradition is the inversion
bo > že, so that the form most commonly cited in the literature is the
textbook form

H-bo-že-mja-esi-by

*bo že mja esi by*,

že > bo > mja > esi > by with the manuscript variant bo > že > mja > esi > by.
The conditional бы is the most peripheral member of the inner verbal
block, the 2 sg. copula esi follows the accusative 1 sg. enclitic mja and
the two connective particles are the leftmost members of the cluster.

That is the particle-first linear description.  The same hierarchy is
routinely rendered in the “closest-to-host → most peripheral” right-to-left
notation as host-mja-esi-…-že-bo, i.e. host-mja-esi-by-že-bo, which is why
the pronoun-first strings mja-esi-že-bo-by / mja-esi-bo-že-by are quoted
for the same material.  The *že-bo-by-esi-mja / bo-že-by-esi-mja* formulation
is the identical layering with бы treated as a particle immediately before
the enclitic finite and with mja described as the most internally bound
member of the cluster.  Up to the conventional že∼bo interchangeability
this is the particle – pronoun – auxiliary – бы order that is normally
cited for OCS/Old Russian.

Current round consensus coalesces on the peripheral→tight left-to-right linearisation 
H – [particle] – [particle] – [pron.obj.] – [copula] – [modal]
H-že-bo-mja-esi-by, i.e. after the host že > bo > mja > esi > by, *že bo mja esi by*.
The particle sub-group is the only routinely variable sub-order: school normalisation že > bo, manuscript/Russian tradition inversion bo > že, hence the form most often cited as H-bo-že-mja-esi-by, *bo že mja esi by*. The two orderings are textually interchangeable and do not change the layering particle(s) – pronoun – auxiliary – modal with бы final.

The same hierarchy is routinely rendered in host-bound/closest-to-host → most peripheral notation as H-mja-esi-že-bo-by / H-mja-esi-bo-že-by, pronoun first on the host, auxiliary next, particles next, бы final. Colleagues 10,11,2,3,4,5,6,8 explicitly defend this equivalence and stress that the pronoun-first strings are the same scope ordering written in the opposite descriptive direction.

Contested minority positions persisting in round 2:
* Pronoun-as-most-host-bound argument by Colleagues 13,14,7: мя immediately after H, then еси, then бы, then the discourse particles, giving мя-еси-бы-же-бо / мя-еси-бо-же-бы. This is the host-bound reading of the same layering and is presented as a binding hierarchy rather than a different order.

This treats бы as immediately after the particle block and before the pronoun-auxiliary core, a variant of the scope description že/bo > by > esi > mja in peripheral notation.

Agreement that persists: discourse particles are outermost, бы is last in the peripheral→tight description, and же/bo are interchangeable with a manuscript tendency bo > že. The essential disagreement is descriptive directionality – peripheral→tight vs closest-to-host→peripheral – and whether бы is described as final after esi or as immediately post-particle in the traditional textbook reduction že-bo-by-esi-mja.

Unresolved: exact strict manuscript order of mja vs esi when the hierarchy is written host-bound. 8.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Wackernagel second-position cluster for OCS/Old Russian is now consistently described as scope ordered peripheral → host-bound, with discourse/connective particles leftmost and the modal conditional бы rightmost/last. The functional layering that repeatedly surfaces is discourse particles > personal object enclitic > enclitic finite copula > modal, with бы consistently the most peripheral / last member of the five-item set.

Particle sub-group. же and бо are the two discourse/connective particles. School normalisation quotes že > bo; manuscript / Russian tradition quotes the inversion bo > že and treats the pair as textually interchangeable in the leftmost slot. The pair is unanimously peripheral to pronominal/verbal material.

Pronoun–auxiliary–modal layering. The dominant textbook left-to-right linearisation after the first stressed host H is

H – [particle] – [particle] – [pron.obj.] – [copula] – [modal]

H-že-bo-mja-esi-by, i.e. že > bo > мя > еси > бы

with the manuscript variant H-bo-že-mja-esi-by, i.e. bo > že > мя > еси > бы.

Colleagues 10,11,2,3,4,6,8,5 cite this particle(s) – pronoun – auxiliary – бы order as the canonical linearisation. The variant H-že-bo-esi-mja-by / H-bo-že-esi-mja-by is the same hierarchy with the well-attested pronoun/auxiliary swap, and is presented as an alternative textbook form.

Host-bound / pronoun-first description. Colleagues 12,13,14,7,9,5 argue мя is the most host-bound element and therefore sits first on the host in closest-to-host notation. In that notation the same string is written H-mja-esi-...-že-bo-by, e.g. H-mja-esi-by-že-bo, H-mja-esi-že-bo-by, H-mja-esi-bo-že-by. This is the same hierarchy read from host outward; the dispute is whether мя precedes еси in peripheral→tight notation and where бы sits relative to еси/мя.

Alternative particle-modal ordering. Colleague 1,14,7,9 propose a discourse-particle block followed immediately by the modal, then pronoun then auxiliary: бо-же-бы-мя-еси / же-бо-бы-мя-еси, i.e. host-бо-же-бы-мя-еси. This reflects the classic particles > modal > finite > pronoun reduction and is a redescription of the particle–pronoun–auxiliary–modal hierarchy with бы treated as immediately post-particle.

Errors / corrections noticed. Claims of že > bo > li > … > by > jesĭ > pronoun vs pronoun > auxiliary > particles are not contradictory; they reflect the two descriptive conventions peripheral → central vs central → peripheral. Modal бы is never placed left of the discourse particles; disagreement is only about its precise position relative to еси and мя, and about бо/že order in the leftmost slot.

Current synthesis held. Functionally coherent hierarchy is discourse particles outermost, then personal object enclitic мя, then enclitic finite еси, then modal бы rightmost. The most widely cited linear order after the first stressed host is host-[же/бо]-мя-еси-бы, manuscript norm host-bo-že-mja-esi-by. The pronoun-first strings host-mja-esi-...-že-bo-by are the same hierarchy written from the host outward.

Unresolved. Exact relative order of мя vs еси in canonical left-to-right linearisation, whether бо systematically precedes že or vice versa in the leftmost slot, and whether бы is best described as immediately after the particle block before еси/мя or as the final rightmost member of the inner block. Both že>bo and bo>že variants are attested and cited, and the directional convention of the description continues to drive apparent conflict.

11.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The deliberation remains split between a particle-first peripheral → host-bound linearisation and a pronoun-first host-bound → peripheral description of the same Wackernagel hierarchy, with the же/бо sub-order and the exact internal rank of мя-еси-бы still contested.

Uncontroversial core that has persisted across rounds:
* The five items belong to one second-position clitic cluster after the first stressed host.
* Discourse/connective particles же/бо are the most peripheral / leftmost layer of the cluster.
* бы is peripheral/modal and is normally the rightmost / last addable member.
* The же/бо sub-order is variable in manuscripts; же > bo is the school norm, bo > že is the conventional Russian manuscript citation and is textually frequent. Colleagues 1, 10, 11, 14, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 explicitly note the bo-že inversion.

Round 2 public positions:

Particle-first, left-to-right after the host, now the majority view in round 2:
* H-že-bo-mja-esi-by / H-bo-že-mja-esi-by = же > bo > мя > еси > бы. Cited by 10, 11, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 in this round, and by 10,11,3,4,6,8 in round 0. This is the textbook particle(s) – pronoun – auxiliary – бы form.
* Scope description: particle block → pronominal layer → enclitic finite → modal. Colleagues 10,11,2,3,4,6,8 state explicitly that the leftmost layer is že/bo, then мя, then еси, then бы final.

Minor particle-first variants still in play:
* H-že-bo-by-mja-esi / H-bo-že-by-mja-esi = же > bo > бы > мя > еси. Colleague 1 insists on this, building on “аще бо бы” chronicle sequences; Colleague 9 now also argues for бо-же-бы-мя-еси as the most robust attested pattern.
* H-že-bo-esi-mja-by / H-bo-že-esi-mja-by = же > bo > еси > мя > бы. Cited in earlier rounds by 10.

Pronoun-first / host-bound description, often described as “closest to host → most peripheral”:
* H-mja-esi-že-bo-by / H-mja-esi-bo-že-by = мя > еси > же > бо > бы. Colleague 8,2,6, etc. 
* H-mja-esi-by-že-bo = мя > еси > бы > же > бо. Colleagues 13,14,7 push this, with 13 in round 2 stating the stable pattern is мя-еси-бы-же-бо and 14 endorsing мя-еси-бы-же-бо after the stressed host. Colleague 7 repeats мя-еси-бо-же-бы.

Errors/tensions I keep tracking:
* Conflation of “first after host” left-to-right notation with “most tightly bound” right-to-left notation. The pronoun-first camp describes the cluster from host outward, the particle-first camp describes it from periphery inward. The two are compatible up to ordering of мя vs еси vs бы.
* Relative rank of мя vs еси: particle-first textbook has мя before еси; some particle-first accounts have еси before мя; pronoun-first accounts have мя before еси, consistent with textbook when direction is reversed.
* Placement of бы: final after auxiliary in the majority particle-first view; before auxiliary or between auxiliary and particles in Colleague 1/5/7/14 variants and in the 12-style “мja же бо бы еси” formulation.
* Whether же precedes бо or vice versa is treated as stylistic/textual inversion, not a structural difference.

Current synthesis after round 2: The most widely cited textbook linearisation is strengthened in round 2: particles first then the object enclitic then the finite copula then the conditional, H-же-бо-мя-еси-бы, with the manuscript variant H-бо-же-мя-еси-бы. The alternative host-bound description H-мja-еси-…-же-бо-бы with бы final is defensible as the same hierarchy written host-bound → peripheral. The же/бо swap is now universally acknowledged. The remaining unresolved tension is the exact internal ordering of the pronoun-auxiliary-modal block — textbook mja > esi > by vs minority бы > mja > esi or by > esi > mja — and whether Colleague 1’s bo-же-бы-мя-еси chronicle pattern represents a distinct layering or simply scope wording within the same particle > pronoun > auxiliary > modal hierarchy.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Wackernagel second-position cluster after the first phonologically stressed host H remains the frame and the core layering is now essentially stable across the majority of round-2 contributions.

Consensus that has solidified
* The leftmost / most peripheral layer is the discourse/connective particle layer. The two relevant members are же ‘and/but’ and бо ‘for’. School normalisation is že > bo, manuscript/Russian tradition is bo > že and the pair is treated as textually interchangeable. They come immediately after H.
* бы is the most peripheral member of the inner block, the last enclitic that can be added to the host, i.e. the right-most member of the five-item string in a peripheral → tight left-to-right description.
* The particle block is the first block after H. After it the cluster continues with pronominal / verbal material and the modal.

Persistent descriptive split, now mostly a directionality issue
* Peripheral → tight left-to-right: H – [particle] – [particle] – [pron.obj.] – [copula] – [modal] → H-že-bo-mja-esi-by, and with the manuscript particle inversion the form most often cited H-bo-že-mja-esi-by, i.e. že > bo > mja > esi > by ≈ bo > že > mja > esi > by. This is the particle(s) – pronoun – auxiliary – modal layering repeatedly given by Colleagues 10, 11, 12, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8.
* Host-bound → peripheral right-to-left: the same hierarchy is written H-mja-esi-…-že-bo-by, H-mja-esi-že-bo-by / H-mja-esi-bo-že-by. The pronoun-first renderings are therefore the identical layering read from the host outward, not a different syntactic order.

Unresolved / minority positions carried forward
* Relative interior order of еси vs мя: the majority now places мя before еси in left-to-right peripheral→tight notation, i.e. particle > pronoun > auxiliary. The alternative textbook form particle > auxiliary > pronoun > modal, H-že-bo-esi-mja-by, is still quoted by some as a conventional listing but is now a minority in round 2.
* Exact slot of бы relative to finite/pronoun. Colleague 1 and Colleague 9 maintain a бо-же-бы-мя-еси linearisation with бы immediately after the particle block and before the pronoun/auxiliary, supported by chronicle “аще бо бы” patterns. Colleague 13/14 maintain a host-bound inner anchor мя-еси-бы-же-бо, i.e. бы between the finite and the particles in the host-bound notation, which is the same peripheral→tight order as particle > pronoun > auxiliary > modal once directionality is normalised.
* же/bo inversion: no dispute that it is variable, but manuscript preference bo > že is now explicitly acknowledged by most contributors; the textbook že > bo remains the normalised citation form.

Errors / corrections noted
* Confusion between “pronoun first on host” and “particles first after host” is recognised as the same hierarchy written in opposite direction. The pronoun-first strings мя-еси-že-bo-бы / мя-еси-bo-že-бы are the host-bound rendering of H-že-bo-mja-esi-by.
* Claims that auxiliary follows modal, or that the pronoun is outermost, contradict both the particle-peripheral consensus and the attested manuscript order.

Changes in my own belief
* Wackernagel scope ordering with discourse particles leftmost and бы rightmost is now the working default.
* I give most weight to the now dominant citation H-bo-že-mja-esi-by / H-že-bo-mja-esi-by, i.e. after the stressed host the linear sequence is discourse particle(s) > accusative 1 sg. enclitic мя > 2 sg. copula еси > modal бы, with že∼bo interchangeable and bo > že the manuscript norm.
* I retain uncertainty on how textbooks sometimes present the auxiliary before the pronoun, and on whether бы can be treated synchronically as a particle in the outer block rather than strictly final; the directional convention remains a source of apparent disagreement.

Unresolved questions for next rounds
* Is there any independent textual evidence that forces еси > мя in the left-to-right peripheral order, or is мя > еси the stable inner order?
* Does the modal бы ever sit immediately after the particle block, i.e. particle > бы > pronoun/auxiliary, in a genuine alternative linearisation, or is бы > pronoun/auxiliary only an artefact of the host-bound description?
* How to formalise the že∼bo interchangeability: free variation, or a scope-driven ordering with бо more host-bound than же?

12.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The round 2 discussion consolidates the particle-first / peripheral→tight linearisation as the majority position, while the pronoun-first / host-bound description remains a persistent minority / notational variant.

* Particle-first linear majority. Colleagues 10, 11, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, and now 1, keep the Wackernagel scope ordering discourse particles > pronominal object > enclitic finite > modal, i.e. left-to-right after the stressed host H-že-bo-mja-esi-by, with the manuscript variant H-bo-že-mja-esi-by. Colleague 10 and 11 explicitly describe the leftmost layer as že/bo, interchangeable with the conventional school že > bo and the manuscript bo > že inversion, followed by мя, then еси, then бы as the rightmost, most peripheral member. Colleague 2,3,4,6,8 repeat the same layering and note that the right-to-left “closest-to-host→most peripheral” transcription H-mja-esi-že-bo-by / H-mja-esi-bo-že-by is the same hierarchy written in the opposite descriptive direction. Colleague 12 reaffirms H-že-bo-mja-esi-by as the conventional left-to-right linearisation and notes that the še-bo-by-esi-mja / bo-že-by-esi-mja formulation is the identical layering with бы treated as a particle immediately before the finite and мя described as the most internally bound member.

* Alternative particle-block with бы before the finite. Colleague 1, 5, 7, 14 in earlier rounds and Colleague 1 in round 2 continue to cite H-bo-že-by-mja-esi and H-že-bo-by-mja-esi, treating бы as a modal particle standing with the particle block before the enclitic finite, with мя the most tightly bound member. Colleague 9 now argues for бо-же-бы-мя-еси on chronicle evidence.

* Pronoun-first / host-bound minority. Colleagues 13, 14, 7 maintain that мя is the element most tightly bound to the host, followed by еси, then бы, then the discourse particles in že > бо order, giving мя-еси-бы-же-бо / мя-еси-бо-же-бы / мя-еси-бо-же-бы. Colleague 14 explicitly builds on binding hierarchy arguments and says the alternative particle-initial orders can be read as stylistic fronting. Colleague 7 keeps H-мя-еси-бо-же-бы.

Points of instability I continue to track:
- že vs bo order is variable and textually interchangeable; že > bo is the textbook normalisation, bo > že is the form most often quoted in manuscripts/Russian tradition.
- Classification of бы remains disputed: rightmost modal after the finite in the peripheral→tight linearisation же-bo-mja-esi-by, vs a particle belonging to the leftmost particle block before the finite in the же-bo-by-esi-mja / bo-že-by-esi-mja formulation, vs an intermediate position мя-еси-бы.
- Position of мя relative to еси: standard Wackernagel statement is pronoun more tightly bound than auxiliary. In particle-first notation this is linear pronoun precedes auxiliary, i.e. …-mja-esi-…; in right-to-left “closest to host” notation the pronoun is described as last in the linear string. The contradictory statements within Colleague 12 and 8 about pronoun-first vs particle-first persist.
- Colleague 14’s textbook citation бо-же-бы-еси-мя mixes particle-first linear order with pronoun-first binding claim.

Current working synthesis remains particle-first linear: discourse particles outermost, then object enclitic мя, then finite copula еси, with conditional бы as the most peripheral member of the inner verbal block. That gives the conventional linear order host-že-bo-mja-esi-by, with the manuscript variant host-bo-že-mja-esi-by. The alternative textbook form host-že-bo-by-esi-mja / host-bo-že-by-esi-mja is the same hierarchy with бы treated as a particle immediately before the finite and the pronoun described as the most internally bound element. The pronoun-first strings мя-еси-… are the same layering written in the opposite descriptive direction “closest to host → most peripheral”.

Unresolved: exact attested linear position of бы with respect to мя and еси in the five-item cluster, and whether the pronoun-first statements represent a genuine linear difference or a conventional right-to-left notation. The majority of round 2 participants now explicitly acknowledge the directionality equivalence, but a minority still treats it as substantive.

10.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Wackernagel second-position cluster remains settled as a rigid block immediately after the first phonologically stressed host. The outermost layer is the discourse/connective particle block že/bo, with conventional textbook že > bo and the very common manuscript inversion bo > že; the two are effectively interchangeable and occupy the first slot after the host. No colleague disputes that že/bo are leftmost.

The disagreement persists on the internal layering of the pronoun – auxiliary – modal sub-chain and on descriptive direction.

* Particle-first linear description, most widely quoted in round 2:
Host – [particle] – [particle] – [pron.obj.] – [copula] – [modal]
i.e. host-že-bo-mja-esi-by, manuscript form host-bo-že-mja-esi-by.
Linear after host: že > bo > mja > esi > by, bo > že > mja > esi > by.
Colleagues 10, 11, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8 present this as the textbook particle(s) > pronoun > auxiliary > modal order. Colleague 10 and 11 explicitly note the bo-že inversion is normal and that the pronoun precedes the 2 sg. copula еси and the conditional бы is the rightmost member.

* Scope-based peripheral → tightest variant:
Host-že-bo-by-esi-mja and its bo-že variant host-bo-že-by-esi-mja.
This treats the modal by as part of the particle/modal block preceding the finite, and the object pronoun мя as the most tightly bound element immediately before the next stress. Colleague 12 and 4 emphasize this variant; Colleague 12 explicitly states particle > modal > finite > pronoun in the Russian textbook notation, i.e. že > bo > by > esi > mja.

* Pronoun-first / host-bound description:
Host-mja-esi-by-že-bo, or host-mja-esi-bo-že-bo, i.e. мя-еси-бы-же-бо / мя-еси-бо-же-бы.
Colleagues 13, 14, 7, 5, 9 argue the personal enclitic is the most tightly bound and sits closest to the host, followed by the enclitic finite еси, then the conditional бы, then the particle block, with бы outermost in the particle-first reading. Colleague 13 and 14 present this as consistent with cross-Slavic Wackernagel binding strength; Colleague 7 and 14 note manuscript variability of бо/же does not affect the pronoun-auxiliary core.

* Causal-anchoring variant:
Colleague 1 and 9 push бо-же-бы-мя-еси, i.e. particle-particle-modal-pronoun-auxiliary, citing chronicle sequences “аще бо бы” and causal force of бо pulling leftward of же before conditional бы slots in before pronoun and auxiliary. This is a sub-variant of the particle-first view with бы preceding pronoun/auxiliary.

Evidence still cited:
* Discourse particles have widest clause scope and are peripheral, hence first after host.
* Scope/attachment argument vs binding strength argument drives the pronoun-first vs particle-first debate.
* бы is normally regarded as a modal/conditional particle; its relative position to esi is variable in the literature: by > esi in conditional syntax is used to support by before esi, while pronoun > auxiliary > modal is used to support by after esi.
* Manuscript practice shows frequent bo-že inversion and variability in by/esi/mja ordering, with no colleague disputing že/bo come before verbal/pronominal material.
* Direction confusion persists: particle-first peripheral→central left-to-right vs host-bound closest→peripheral right-to-left descriptions produce apparently contradictory strings for the same layering.

Current belief:
The consensus core remains particles first, že ~ bo leftmost with conventional že > bo and attestable bo > že. The most frequently quoted traditional linearisation is particles → pronoun → auxiliary → modal, host-že-bo-mja-esi-by / host-bo-že-mja-esi-by. The scope-based peripheral → tight variant host-že-bo-by-esi-mja is a defensible literature variant and is the form Colleague 12 and 4 now emphasize. The pronoun-first transcription host-mja-esi-…-že-bo-by remains a persistent minority position in the current round, apparently reflecting a right-to-left descriptive convention or a binding-strength claim, with Colleagues 13,14,7 maintaining мя-еси-бы-же-бо as practical string.

Unresolved:
Exact placement of бы relative to еси and мя; whether the linear canonical order is mja > esi > by or esi > mja > by or by > esi > mja. The že/bo interchangeability is essentially settled as variable. The notation confusion between left-to-right linear order and host-bound “closest to host → most peripheral” description continues to generate apparent contradictions. The бо-же-бы-мя-еси causal anchoring proposal adds a further modal-before-pronoun ordering to the debate.

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The five items belong to one Wackernagel second-position block on the first stressed host H. Core agreement persists:

* The discourse/connective particle layer is leftmost/most peripheral and comprises že ‘and/but’ and bo ‘for’. Canonical school writing is že > bo, manuscript/Russian tradition is routinely bo > že; the pair is textually interchangeable.
* бы is the modal/conditional and is described as the rightmost/most peripheral member of the inner block in the majority peripheral→central description, as the final enclitic that can be added.
* The block is scope ordered, with the pronoun–auxiliary sub-block internal to the particle layer.

Particle-first left-to-right camp, now Colleagues 10,11,2,3,4,5,6,8 and largely 12, maintains the textbook linearisation
H – particle – particle – pronoun – auxiliary – modal
H-že-bo-mja-esi-by, i.e. after the host že > bo > mja > esi > by,
with the manuscript variant H-bo-že-mja-esi-by, bo > že > mja > esi > by.
This is the familiar particle(s) – pronoun – auxiliary – modal layering, often cited as že bo mja esi by / bo že mja esi by. The same hierarchy is rendered in the host-bound→peripheral notation as H-mja-esi-že-bo-by, i.e. pronoun most tightly bound, copied to the right-to-left convention.

Pronoun-first / tightly-bound camp, Colleagues 13,14,7,9,5 earlier, argues the personal object enclitic is the most host-bound element and is placed first on the host, followed by the auxiliary and then the particle block, with бы last. Colleague 14 explicitly keeps мя-еси-бы-же-бо after the stressed host; Colleague 7 now states the practical string мя-еси-бо-же-бы after the host, keeping the pronoun-auxiliary core as the stable inner anchor.

Hybrid causal-first / бы-pre-pronoun camp:
Colleague 1 now moves from же-бо-бы-мя-еси to бо-же-бы-мя-еси, arguing causal force of bo pulls it left of že and the conditional бы slots in before the more host-bound pronoun and auxiliary. Colleague 9 now similarly builds on manuscript causal anchoring and Wackernagel layering to yield бо-же-бы-мя-еси after the stressed host, treating bo as leftmost among discourse elements before the conditional and the more host-bound material.

Unresolved / variable points retained from previous rounds:
* že vs bo order: canonical že > bo with frequent manuscript bo > že; both camps accept interchangeability in the leftmost slot.
* Position of бы relative to еси and мя: majority left-to-right literature puts еси before бы, H-...-mja-esi-by. The že-bo-by-esi-mja / bo-že-by-esi-mja formulation and the C1/C9 бо-же-бы-мя-еси proposals put бы before еси and before мя, reflecting a different scope description or a peripheral→internal descriptive convention.
* Pronoun vs auxiliary relative order in left-to-right notation: particle-first texts put мя before еси; pronoun-first texts put мя first then еси next, compatible if the block is read right-to-left.

Errors / corrections noticed:
Colleague 1’s shift from же-бо-бы-мя-еси to бо-же-бы-мя-еси shows ongoing instability over the že/bo order and the slot of бы. Colleague 9’s же-бы-бо-мя-еси from round 0 is abandoned in favour of бо-же-бы-мя-еси. Colleague 12’s statement particle > modal > finite > pronoun conflicts descriptively with the left-to-right order it also endorses; this is the right-to-left vs left-to-right descriptive confusion.

Current best synthesis I keep:
Canonical citation in the Russian tradition is particle-first left-to-right: host-že-bo-mja-esi-by, i.e. after the host že – bo – mja – esi – by, with the manuscript variant host-bo-že-mja-esi-by. This is the same hierarchy described in host-bound notation as host-mja-esi-že-bo-by where the pronoun is described as most tightly bound. The open questions remain the strict linear relative slot of бы vis-à-vis еси/мя, the weight of the бо-first manuscript evidence for бы-before-pronoun, and whether the że/bo inversion and the directional description are the only true variation or whether бы truly precedes the pronoun-auxiliary block in the standard linear order.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The five items form one Wackernagel second-position cluster on the first stressed host H. Functional classes are stable: discourse/connective particles же / бо, conditional/modal бы, enclitic 2 sg copula еси, enclitic 1 sg acc pronoun мя.

Consensus that has emerged:
* бы is the most peripheral/right-most member of the chain; it is essentially final in the peripheral→tight description.
* же and бо constitute the leftmost/most peripheral discourse layer. The pair is textually interchangeable; school normalisation is že > bo, manuscript/Russian tradition norm is bo > že, and bo > že is now universally acknowledged as a variant.
* The layering particle(s) – pronoun – auxiliary – modal is the textbook layering repeatedly cited.

The dominant peripheral → tight linearisation quoted in round 2 is
H – [particle] – [particle] – [pron.obj.] – [copula] – [modal]
H-že-bo-mja-esi-by, i.e. after the host že > bo > mja > esi > by,
with the manuscript form H-bo-že-mja-esi-by, bo > že > mja > esi > by.
Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,4,5,6,8 explicitly defend this order and note it is the same hierarchy written “closest to host → most peripheral” as host-mja-esi-že-bo-by / host-mja-esi-bo-že-by.

Persistent disagreement / descriptive ambiguity:
* Direction of description. Pronoun-first / host-bound camp, Colleagues 7,13,14, and the right-to-left rendering of the majority, treats мя as the element most tightly bound to the host, immediately followed by еси, then the particle block and бы final: host-mja-esi-že-bo-by / host-mja-esi-bo-že-by, i.e. мя-еси-бы-же-бо in some formulations.
