reflection_text.2:
The Wackernagel second-position cluster after the first phonologically stressed host H remains the frame and the core layering is now essentially stable across the majority of round-4 contributions, with the directionality/peripheral→tight vs host-bound→peripheral confusion still accounting for most apparent disagreement.

Consensus that has solidified
* Leftmost / most peripheral layer is the discourse/connective particle layer. Members are же ‘and/but’ and бо ‘for’. School normalisation is že > bo, manuscript/Russian tradition is bo > že and the pair is treated as textually interchangeable. They come immediately after H.
* Particle block is the first block after H. After it the cluster continues with pronominal / verbal material.
* Majority peripheral→tight left-to-right description: H – [particle] – [particle] – [pron.obj.] – [copula] – [modal] → H-že-bo-mja-esi-by, and with manuscript particle inversion the form most often cited H-bo-že-mja-esi-by, i.e. že > bo > mja > esi > by ≈ bo > že > mja > esi > by. This is repeatedly given by Colleagues 10, 11, 12, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, and affirmed in round 4 by 10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8.
* бы is treated by the majority as the most peripheral member of the inner block, the right-most member of the five-item string in peripheral→tight notation. Pronoun-first renderings H-mja-esi-by-že-bo / H-mja-esi-bo-že-by are the same hierarchy written host-bound→peripheral, closest-to-host → most peripheral, not a different syntactic order.

Persistent descriptive split, now mostly a scope / linearisation issue
* Peripheral→tight left-to-right: particle(s) – pronoun – auxiliary – modal. 
* Host-bound→peripheral right-to-left: pronoun-first strings мя-еси-…-že-bo-by. Colleagues 13/6/8 note pronoun as most host-bound.

Unresolved / minority positions carried forward
* Particle-particle-modal-pronoun-auxiliary: Colleagues 1,5,7,9,14 now strongly push бо-же-бы-мя-еси as best fit with chronicle evidence, e.g. “аще бо бы” strings and documented leftward pull of causal бо in explanatory contexts. Argument: бо anchors left of же, бы slots immediately after the discourse block before the more tightly bound pronoun-auxiliary pair. This preserves outer-to-inner scope and explains manuscript flexibility without extra assumptions. Colleague 14 in round 4 now frames this as particle-initial cluster бо же мя еси бы, i.e. still particle-initial but with бы before pronoun in the minority reading.
* Pronoun-first binding hierarchy: Colleague 13 maintains most stable pattern мя immediately after stressed host, followed by еси then бы then discourse particles → мя-еси-бы-же-бо, arguing host-bound core is violated by rigidly peripheral particle placement.
* Relative interior order of еси vs мя: majority now places мя before еси in left-to-right peripheral→tight notation, i.e. particle > pronoun > auxiliary. Alternative textbook particle > auxiliary > pronoun > modal is minority.

Errors / corrections noted
* Confusion between “pronoun first on host” and “particles first after host” is recognised as same hierarchy written opposite direction. Pronoun-first strings мя-еси-že-bo-бы / мя-еси-bo-že-бы are host-bound rendering of H-že-bo-mja-esi-by.
* Claims that auxiliary follows modal, or that pronoun is outermost, contradict particle-peripheral consensus and attested manuscript order.

Changes in my own belief
* Wackernagel scope ordering with discourse particles leftmost and бы rightmost in peripheral→tight notation remains working default.
* Most weight still goes to dominant citation H-bo-že-mja-esi-by / H-že-bo-mja-esi-by, i.e. after stressed host linear sequence is discourse particle(s) > accusative 1 sg. enclitic мя > 2 sg. copula еси > modal бы, with že∼bo interchangeable and bo > že manuscript norm.
* The chronicle “бо бы” evidence raised repeatedly by C1, C5, C7, C9, C14 has increased uncertainty about exact slot of бы: whether бы is strictly final after еси or can synchronically be positioned immediately after particle block, бы > pronoun/auxiliary, in genuine alternative linearisation. Majority in round 4 treats “аще бо бы” as stylistic fronting within outer discourse layer, not movement of бы ahead of pronoun-auxiliary core.

Unresolved questions for next rounds
* Is there independent textual evidence that forces еси > мя in left-to-right peripheral order, or is мя > еси stable inner order?
* Does modal бы ever sit immediately after the particle block, i.e. particle > бы > pronoun/auxiliary, in a genuine alternative linearisation, or is бы > pronoun/auxiliary only artefact of host-bound description / chronicle stylistic fronting?
* How to formalise že∼bo interchangeability: free variation, or scope-driven ordering with бо more host-bound than же?

Earlier important points retained: second-position cluster is scope ordered peripheral → more host-bound; pronoun is most tightly bound in host-bound description; discourse particles are outermost; бы is final in conventional peripheral→tight description; manuscript norm is bo > že.
reflection_text.8:
The Wackernagel second-position cluster for OCS/Old Russian is scope ordered peripheral → host-bound, conventionally written peripheral → tight left-to-right after the first stressed host H.

Peripheral outermost layer = discourse/connective particle layer. Members že ‘and/but’ and bo ‘for’. School normalisation quotes že > bo; manuscript / Russian tradition regularly shows the inversion bo > že and treats the pair as textually interchangeable in the leftmost slot. The pair is unanimously peripheral to pronominal/verbal material.

After the particle block comes the pronominal layer, acc. 1 sg. object enclitic мя, which precedes the enclitic finite. Next comes the enclitic finite, 2 sg. copula еси, which follows мя. Modal/conditional бы is the most peripheral member of the inner block, i.e. the right-most member of the five-item chain in peripheral→tight notation.

Hence the dominant textbook linearisation after H is

H-[particle]-[particle]-[pron.obj.]-[cop.]-[modal]
H-že-bo-mja-esi-by  →  že > bo > мя > еси > бы
manuscript norm H-bo-že-mja-esi-by → bo > že > мя > еси > бы

Host-bound → peripheral transcriptions H-mja-esi-…-že-bo-by are the same hierarchy written closest-to-host → most peripheral; the dispute is descriptive directionality, not a different order.

Competing proposals in round 4:
* Chronically-attested particle-initial modal adjacency: C1, C5, C7, C9, C14, now C1 again, argue бо-же-бы-мя-еси / же-бо-бы-мя-еси from repeated chronicle clusters “аще бо бы” and the claim that causal bo anchors left of že and бы slots immediately after the discourse block before the pronoun-auxiliary core. They treat particle-initial strings as the canonical order and view pronoun-first renderings as stylistic fronting or descriptive reversals.
* Binding-hierarchy minority: C13 maintains the strongest host-bound element is the personal enclitic, yielding мя-еси-бы-же-бо / мя-еси-бы-же-бо, i.e. pronoun → auxiliary → modal → particles, with particles treated as stylistically frontable.

Arguments for and against:
For particle > pronoun > auxiliary > modal with бы final: C10, C11, C12, C2, C3, C4, C6, C8 consistently reaffirm scope layering discourse particles > pronoun > auxiliary > modal, with бы right-most and že∼bo interchangeable, and dismiss бо-же-бы-мя-еси as explanatory particle-modal collocation inside the outer discourse layer, not a reordering of the full five-member chain.
Against: C1, C5, C7, C9, C14 counter that the same manuscripts routinely show бо first in explanatory contexts and бы immediately after the particle block, and that requiring бы to be final forces overriding of those attested “аще бо бы” clusters.

Errors / corrections noticed: Claims of že > bo > li > … > by > jesĭ > pronoun vs pronoun > auxiliary > particles are not contradictory; they reflect peripheral→central vs central→peripheral descriptive convention. Modal бы is never placed left of the discourse particles; disagreement is only about its precise position relative to еси/мя and about бо/že order in the leftmost slot. The že∼bo interchangeability is stylistic/textual; the modal бы remains final in the majority peripheral→tight view.

Current synthesis held: Functionally coherent hierarchy is discourse particles outermost, then personal object enclitic мя, then enclitic finite еси, then modal бы rightmost. Most widely cited linear order after H is host-[же/бо]-мя-еси-бы, manuscript norm host-bo-že-mja-esi-by. Pronoun-first strings host-mja-esi-…-že-bo-by are the same hierarchy read from host outward.

Unresolved: Exact relative order of мя vs еси in canonical left-to-right linearisation is stable in the majority as мя > еси, but some textbook variants swap them; exact бо/že order remains variable, bo > že being the conventional manuscript norm; and whether бы is best described as immediately after the particle block before pronoun-auxiliary, as in бо-же-бы-мя-еси, or as final rightmost member after еси, as in бо-же-мя-еси-бы, remains the live dispute, compounded by directionality convention differences.
reflection_text.4:
The five items form one Wackernagel second-position block on the first stressed host H. Core agreement persists on scope layering: discourse/connective particle layer outermost, then pronominal, then enclitic finite, then modal/conditional, with the only stable sub-variation being že ~ bo interchangeability: school normalisation že > bo, manuscript/Russian tradition routinely bo > že, both camps treat the pair as textually interchangeable and leftmost after H.

Majority particle-first left-to-right camp, Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8, maintains canonical linearisation H – particle – particle – pron.obj. – cop. – modal
H-že-bo-mja-esi-by, i.e. after host že > bo > мя > еси > бы, with manuscript variant H-bo-že-mja-esi-by, bo > že > мя > еси > бы. This is particle(s) – pronoun – auxiliary – modal, бы rightmost/final. The same hierarchy is routinely rendered in host-bound → peripheral right-to-left notation as H-mja-esi-že-bo-by / H-mja-esi-bo-že-by.

Colleague 4 has now moved to this majority description,放弃 earlier že > bo > by > esi > mja formulation, explicitly stating peripheral → more host-bound discourse/connective > pronoun > finite > modal and citing H-že-bo-mja-esi-by / H-bo-že-mja-esi-by.

Pronoun-first / tightly-bound camp, Colleague 13 remains, now explicitly мя-еси-бы-же-бо, arguing мя immediately after host, followed by еси then бы, then particles. Colleagues 2,3,6,8 also quote the same hierarchy in host-bound notation, but interpret it as the same peripheral → tight order.

Hybrid causal-first / бы-pre-pronoun camp, Colleagues 1,5,7,9 now converge on бо-же-бы-мя-еси, arguing causal бо reliably initiates discourse layer, же follows, conditional бы slots immediately afterward because syntactically linked to ensuing verbal material before the more host-bound pronoun-auxiliary pair. C1, C5, C7, C9 cite chronicle clusters “аще бо бы” as evidence for particle-conditional adjacency and leftward pull of бо. C5 and C7 stress that textbook particle-pronoun-auxiliary-modal layering would require overriding those passages.

Colleague 14 is now intermediate: it endorses Wackernagel scope layering and the bo > že manuscript inversion, and favours particle-initial cluster бо же мя еси бы as most economical, stating pronoun-auxiliary follows before modal closes string. This is consistent with the majority particle > pronoun > auxiliary > modal order, not with бо-же-бы-мя-еси, though C14 continues to cite “аще бо бы”.

Unresolved / variable points retained:
* že vs bo order: canonical že > bo with frequent manuscript bo > že; both accepted as interchangeable in leftmost slot.
* Position of бы relative to еси and мя: majority left-to-right puts еси before бы, бы final; the бо-же-бы-мя-еси proposals put бы before мя-еси; the earlier že-bo-by-esi-mja formulation also put бы before esi/mja.
* Pronoun vs auxiliary relative order in left-to-right notation: particle-first texts put мя before еси; pronoun-first texts describe мя first then еси next, compatible if block is read right-to-left.
* Descriptive direction confusion persists: host-bound → peripheral transcriptions H-mja-esi-...-že-bo-by are the same hierarchy written closest-to-host → most peripheral.

Errors/corrections noticed:
Colleague 4’s shift from the že > bo > by > esi > mja descriptive formulation to the majority že > bo > мя > еси > бы formulation; Colleague 12 explicitly dismisses бо-же-бы-мя-еси as stylistic fronting within particle block, not evidence for moving бы ahead of pronoun-auxiliary core.

Current best synthesis I keep:
Canonical citation in the Russian tradition remains particle-first left-to-right: host-že-bo-mja-esi-by, i.e. after host že – bo – мя – еси – бы, with manuscript variant host-bo-že-mja-esi-by. This is the same hierarchy described in host-bound notation as host-mja-esi-že-bo-by where pronoun is described as most tightly bound. Open questions remain the strict linear relative slot of бы vis-à-vis еси/мя, the weight of the бо-first manuscript evidence for бы-before-pronoun-auxiliary, and whether že/bo inversion and directional description are the only true variation or whether бы truly precedes the pronoun-auxiliary block in the standard linear order.
reflection_text.6:
The five enclitics form one Wackernagel second-position cluster on the first stressed host H. Functional classes are stable: discourse/connective particles же/бо, conditional/modal бы, enclitic 2sg copula еси, enclitic 1sg acc pronoun мя.

Consensus that has held through rounds:
* Discourse particle layer is leftmost/peripheral after H. же and бо are textually interchangeable; school normalisation že > bo, manuscript/Russian tradition norm bo > že.
* Layering in conventional peripheral→tight left-to-right notation is particle(s) – pronoun – auxiliary – modal.
* бы is the most peripheral inner member, right-most in peripheral→tight description; majority keeps бы final after еси.
* Pronoun-first transcriptions H-mja-esi-…-že-bo-by are the same hierarchy written host-bound→peripheral, closest-to-host→most peripheral.

Round 4 positions:
Peripheral→tight majority C10, C11, C12, C2, C3, C4, C6, C8:
H-[particle]-[particle]-[pron.obj.]-[cop.]-[modal]
H-že-bo-mja-esi-by i.e. after host že > bo > мя > еси > бы
Manuscript form H-bo-že-mja-esi-by i.e. bo > že > мя > еси > бы
They stress scope ordering peripheral>more host-bound, particle block leftmost, мя precedes еси in left-to-right appearance, бы final, and že∼bo interchangeability is the only normal variation. Host-bound→peripheral renderings H-mja-esi-že-bo-by / H-mja-esi-bo-že-by are described as descriptive reversals, not a different order.

Modal-intervention minority C1, C5, C7, C9, C14:
Defends бо-же-бы-мя-еси, i.e. particle block then бы before pronoun-auxiliary block. Evidence repeatedly invoked: chronicle clusters аще бо бы, causal anchoring of бо left of же, explanatory contexts where бо pulls leftward and бы follows particles immediately before more host-bound pronoun-auxiliary pair. They treat бы as intervening between particle block and pronoun/auxiliary, not final after auxiliary. Бо-first inversion is taken as normative.

Binding-hierarchy minority C13:
Argues for tightest binding = pronoun first after host: мя-еси-бы-же-бо / мя-еси-бы-же-бо, with pronoun immediately after H, then еси, then бы, then discourse particles. Claims pronoun-auxiliary core precedes particles in manuscripts, and that particle-initial renderings are stylistic fronting.

Persistent disagreement:
Direction of description/binding strength. Pronoun-first/host-bound camp vs peripheral→tight camp. Colleague 13 explicitly argues мя-еси-бы-же-бо.

Modal placement. Whether бы is final after еси as in particle > pronoun > auxiliary > modal, or whether бы sits immediately after the particle block before pronoun-auxiliary as in бо-же-бы-мя-еси.

Relative rank of мя vs еси inside pronoun-auxiliary sub-block depends on descriptive direction; peripheral→tight gives мя > еси left-to-right, host-bound gives мя before еси closest to host.

Evidence repeatedly invoked across rounds: manuscript frequency bo-že over že-bo; chronicle аще бо бы; scope argument discourse particles > pronoun > auxiliary > modal; binding argument personal enclitic pronoun most host-bound.

Unresolved points remaining: exact linear rank of мя vs еси inside pronoun-auxiliary sub-block under a single convention; whether бы intervenes between particle block and pronoun/auxiliary or is final after auxiliary; whether бо-же-бы-мя-еси represents a distinct layering or a descriptive variant of particle-pronoun-auxiliary-modal with scope-based modal placement. Bo/že inversion and the existence of a fixed Wackernagel cluster are essentially consensus; dispute is descriptive direction and modal vs pronoun/auxiliary ordering.
reflection_text.10:
The Wackernagel second-position cluster remains a rigid block immediately after the first phonologically stressed host. The outermost layer is settled as the discourse/connective particle block že/bo, with school normalisation že > bo and the well-attested manuscript inversion bo > že; the two are effectively interchangeable and leftmost. No colleague disputes že/bo come first.

The disagreement is now framed as descriptive direction plus the internal ordering of pronoun – auxiliary – modal.

* Particle-first peripheral → tight linearisation, still the most widely quoted:
Host – [particle] – [particle] – [pron.obj.] – [cop.] – [modal]
i.e. host-že-bo-mja-esi-by, manuscript norm host-bo-že-mja-esi-by.
že > bo > mja > esi > by ; bo > že > mja > esi > by.
Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8 state this explicitly in round 4 and note that the pronoun-first transcriptions host-mja-esi-…-že-bo-by are the same hierarchy written closest-to-host → most peripheral, i.e. a right-to-left descriptive reversal. Colleague 10 now also acknowledges the common rendering by immediately before the finite, i.e. že-bo-by-esi-mja / bo-že-by-esi-mja, as a variant of the same scope layering.

* Scope-based peripheral → tight variant with modal before finite and pronoun most internal:
Host-že-bo-by-esi-mja and host-bo-že-by-esi-mja.
Particle > modal > finite > pronoun. Colleague 12 and 4 continue to emphasise this; Colleague 12 explicitly states particle > modal > finite > pronoun in the Russian textbook notation, i.e. že > bo > by > esi > mja.

* Causal-anchoring particle-initial variant:
bo-že-by-mja-esi, i.e. particle-particle-modal-pronoun-auxiliary.
Colleagues 1,5,7,9,14 in round 4 double down on this, citing chronicle strings “аще бо бы” and the causal leftward pull of бо. They treat бы as slotting in immediately after the discourse particles and before the more host-bound pronoun-auxiliary pair, preserving outer-to-inner scope layering and the documented bo-first inversion without special pleading for binding strength.

* Pronoun-bound / host-bound description:
Host-mja-esi-by-že-bo, i.e. mja-esi-by-že-bo / mja-esi-bo-že-bo.
Colleague 13 maintains the most stable pattern is pronoun most tightly bound to host, then finite auxiliary еси, then conditional бы, then discourse particles же > bo. Colleague 13 argues particle-first citations are stylistic fronting and that the core pronoun-auxiliary-modal layering is fixed in witnesses. Colleagues 2,3,6,8 continue to describe the same hierarchy from the host outward as pronoun > auxiliary > particles, with бы final in the peripheral → tight description.

Evidence still cited:
* Discourse particles have widest clause scope and are peripheral, hence first after host.
* Manuscript practice shows frequent bo-že inversion and variability in by/esi/mja ordering, with no dispute that že/bo are leftmost.
* Chronicle evidence for “аще бо бы” is used by C1/C5/C7/C9/C14 to anchor бо left of же and бы immediately after particles, before pronoun/auxiliary.
* Scope/attachment argument vs binding-strength argument drives pronoun-first vs particle-first debate.
* Direction confusion persists: peripheral → central left-to-right vs host-bound closest → peripheral right-to-left descriptions generate apparently contradictory strings.

Current belief:
Consensus core remains particles first, že ~ bo leftmost with conventional že > bo and attestable bo > že. The traditional textbook linearisation particles → pronoun → auxiliary → modal, host-že-bo-mja-esi-by / host-bo-že-mja-esi-by, is the most frequently quoted and is now explicitly reconciled with pronoun-first transcriptions as a descriptive reversal. The scope variant že-bo-by-esi-mja and the causal anchoring бо-же-бы-мя-еси are defensible literature variants, with the latter particularly tied to chronicle explanatory contexts and the former to modal-before-finite scope readings. The strict pronoun-first мja-еси-бы-же-бо remains a persistent minority position, largely maintained by Colleague 13 and interpretable as the same hierarchy described from the opposite direction.

Unresolved:
Exact placement of бы relative to еси and мя. Whether the canonical linear order is mja > esi > by, esi > mja > by, by > esi > mja, or by > mja > esi. The že/bo interchangeability is essentially settled as variable. Direction notation confusion continues to generate apparent contradictions, and the weight of chronicle “бо бы” clusters versus binding-strength pronoun-first claims is still in balance.
reflection_text.3:
The Wackernagel second-position cluster remains scope ordered peripheral → more host-bound on the first stressed host H.

Stable functional layering in conventional peripheral→tight left-to-right notation is

discourse/connective particle layer > personal object enclitic > enclitic finite auxiliary > modal/conditional

H – [particle] – [particle] – [pron.obj.] – [cop.] – [modal]

H-že-bo-mja-esi-by i.e. after the host že > bo > мя > еси > бы,
… že bo mja esi by …

The two discourse particles are textually interchangeable. School normalisation is že > bo; the Russian manuscript tradition regularly shows the inversion bo > že, the form most often cited is

H-bo-že-mja-esi-by
… бо же мя еси бы …
bo > že > мя > еси > бы.

reflection_text.12:
The deliberation remains centred on the Wackernagel second-position scope ordering peripheral → host-bound after the first stressed host H, with the only stable sub-variation being the textual interchangeability of the two discourse particles že ∼ bo, school normalisation že > bo, manuscript/Russian tradition bo > že.

Particle-first peripheral → tight majority. Colleagues 10, 11, 12, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 repeatedly state the linearisation H-[particle]-[particle]-[pron.obj.]-[cop.]-[modal] i.e. after H že > bo > мя > еси > бы, manuscript variant H-bo-že-mja-esi-by … бо же мя еси бы. The layering is discourse/connective particle layer > personal object enclitic мя > enclitic finite еси > modal/conditional бы, with бы the right-most member of the five-item chain. Directionality equivalence is now explicit: the host-bound → peripheral transcriptions H-mja-esi-…-že-bo-by / H-mja-esi-bo-že-by are the same hierarchy written closest-to-host → most peripheral. Colleague 12 explicitly argues that chronicle clusters “аще бо бы” are stylistic fronting within the particle block and do not require moving бы ahead of the pronoun-auxiliary core.

бы-position dispute. Colleagues 1, 5, 7, 9 continue to push бо-же-бы-мя-еси as the most economical fit with chronicle evidence, treating бо as leftward-anchored in explanatory contexts, же next, бы immediately after the particle block and before the more host-bound pronoun-auxiliary pair мя-еси. They cite “аще бо бы” and similar strings as requiring conditional adjacency to the particles. Colleague 14 in round 4 moves back toward the majority, endorsing the particle-initial cluster бо же мя еси бы with бы final, interpreting “аще бо бы” as discourse particles anchoring leftmost with the modal closing the string.

Pronoun-first / host-bound minority. Colleague 13 remains on the binding-hierarchy position мя immediately after H, then еси, then бы, then discourse particles же-бо, i.e. мя-еси-бы-же-бо, arguing the pronoun-auxiliary core precedes particles in manuscripts and that particle-initial renderings are stylistic fronting. No new support for this view appeared in round 4; the majority treats it as a descriptive reversal rather than a different linear order.

Points of instability I continue to track:
- že vs bo order is variable and textually interchangeable; bo > že is the form most often quoted in manuscripts.
- Classification of бы remains disputed: rightmost modal after the finite in the peripheral → tight linearisation же-bo-mja-esi-by / bo-že-mja-esi-by, vs бы as a particle immediately after the discourse block before мя-еси in the бо-же-бы-мя-еси bloc.
- Position of мя relative to еси is agreed in the canonical left-to-right notation as мя preceding еси; disagreement is purely descriptive directionality.
- Directionality equivalence is widely acknowledged by the particle-first majority, but the бо-же-бы-мя-еси bloc still treats it as a genuine linear difference.

Current working synthesis remains particle-first linear with scope peripheral → tight: discourse particles outermost, then object enclitic мя, then finite copula еси, with conditional бы as the most peripheral member of the inner verbal block: conventional H-že-bo-mja-esi-by, manuscript variant H-bo-že-mja-esi-by. The alternative бо-же-бы-мя-еси is the persistent minority candidate grounded in chronicle “аще бо бы” strings. Unresolved is whether those chronicle clusters reflect a genuine linear placement of бы before мя-еси or stylistic fronting within the peripheral particle layer with бы final.
reflection_text.11:
The five items form one Wackernagel second-position cluster on the first stressed host H, scope layered peripheral → more host-bound.

Core that persists:
* Discourse/connective particle layer is leftmost after H. Members же ‘and/but’ and бо ‘for’ are interchangeable; school normalisation quotes же > бо, Russian manuscript tradition regularly cites the inversion bo > že. They are the most peripheral members.
* After the particle block comes the pronominal layer: acc.1sg. object enclitic мя follows particles and precedes the enclitic finite.
* Next is the enclitic finite: 2sg. copula еси follows мя.
* бы is modal/conditional and is the right-most member of the five-item chain in peripheral→tight left-to-right notation, i.e. the last enclitic that can be added to the host.

In conventional peripheral→tight notation:
H – [particle] – [particle] – [pron.obj.] – [cop.] – [modal]
H-že-bo-mja-esi-by = же > bo > мя > еси > бы
with manuscript variant H-bo-že-mja-esi-by = bo > že > мя > еси > бы.

Host-bound → peripheral transcriptions H-mja-esi-…-že-bo-by, H-mja-esi-že-bo-by / H-mja-esi-bo-že-by are the same hierarchy written closest-to-host → most peripheral.

Current split:

Majority particle-initial / бы-final camp: C10, C11, C12, C2, C3, C4, C6, C8, and now C14. They maintain particle(s) > мя > еси > бы with že ~ bo interchangeable and bo > že as manuscript norm. C12, C6, C8 explicitly rebut the chronicle challenge: strings like “аще бо бы” are stylistic fronting / particle-modal collocations inside the outer discourse layer and do not require moving бы before the pronoun-auxiliary core; pronoun-first strings are descriptive reversals, not a different binding strength.

Minority chronicle conditional-insertion camp: C1, C5, C7, C9. They continue to argue for бо-же-бы-мя-еси / же-бо-бы-мя-еси, i.e. causal бо anchors leftmost, же follows in the interchangeable particle block, and conditional бы slots immediately after the particles before the more host-bound мя-еси pair. Argument rests on attested East Slavic explanatory clusters “аще бо бы” and leftward pull of бо.

Host-bound pronoun-first camp: C13. Maintains the stable pattern мя-еси-бы-же-бо, pronoun immediately after H, then еси, then бы, then discourse particles же > бо, treating particle-initial citations as stylistic fronting. C13 treats this as substantive ordering, not just notational reversal.

Tensions still tracked:
* Conflation of left-to-right peripheral→tight notation with right-to-left host-bound→peripheral notation. Majority treats pronoun-first as notational variant; C13 treats it as substantive.
* Relative rank мя vs еси: textbook has мя before еси; host-bound descriptions keep мя > еси.
* Placement of бы: majority holds бы final after еси; minority chronicle holds бы immediately after particle block, before мя-еси.
* Direction of же/бо: now universally acknowledged as variable; bo > že is conventional manuscript norm.

Changes since previous round: C14 now converges to particle-initial бо же мя еси бы as the most economical fit, abandoning the explicit бы-insertion claim. C12, C6, C8 provide explicit arguments that chronicle “бо бы” examples do not necessitate moving бы ahead of the pronoun-auxiliary core. C1, C5, C7, C9 remain on the бо-же-бы-мя-еси line. C13 remains isolated on мя-еси-бы-же-бо.

Unresolved: whether the textbook particle > pronoun > auxiliary > modal layering with бы final, H-bo-že-mja-esi-by, is the best linearisation, or whether chronicle evidence requires бы to be inserted between the particle block and the pronoun-auxiliary block, yielding бо-же-бы-мя-еси. The majority textbook layering remains the most widely cited descriptive norm with explicit acknowledgment of bo/že interchangeability and notation equivalence, while the chronicle-based challenge that бы should follow the particles immediately before the pronoun-auxiliary block persists but is now explicitly countered as stylistic fronting within the outer layer.
